📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that while you can find plenty of deals on older headphone models during Black Friday sales, it’s rare to see a record-low price and a nearly 30% discount on newer, highly rated models from top brands. That’s exactly why this deal on the critically praised Beats 360 headphones should be on your radar. They’re now down to $249 (originally $349.99) in Amazon’s early Black Friday sale.

Sources indicate that with a design that looks like the love child of the AirPods Max and the Beats Studio Pro, these have an adjustable telescoping frame and a unique modular design that lets you mix and match ear pad colors. The color-swapping bundle isn’t currently on sale, but it’s reassuring to know you can replace the ear pads as they wear out.

They’re controlled by two buttons on each earcup and powered by a dedicated Beats chip, with support for both Android devices and iPhones. You can switch noise modes and, on an iPhone, activate features like Personalized Spatial Audio in Settings. They last up to 32 hours with ANC on, which is longer than both the more expensive Sony WH-1000XM6 and AirPods Max 2.

According to Beats, the 360 offer up to 1.75 times the noise cancellation of the Beats Studio Pro. PCMag’s review, which gave the headphones an “Excellent” rating, was impressed by how well they blocked out everything from plane engine noise to café chatter. The noise cancellation falls short of pricier models, and PCMag found the Sony WH-1000XM4C slightly better in that respect.

The PCMag review notes the headphones deliver “nice, deep bass, reasonably crisp highs, and a more neutral tuning than you might expect for a pair of Beats headphones.” If you’re after long battery life, rich audio, and plush earcups you can swap for a pop of color, $249 is a great price for the Beats 360 headphones.

#131648. Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (882 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
  • EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
  • According to recent reports, motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title. Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI. "My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either." This isn't new to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very swiftly removed after some owners managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices. Derek Rae, one of the currently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, said he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that.".

3 fool-proof steps I use every winter to keep rats out of my shed and yard

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, rats don't hibernate during the winter months, instead they desperately seek out warm shelter.
  • Sources indicate that it's the perfect spot for rats to take up residence and once they find somewhere they like, they'll stick around and populate.
  • Recent findings suggest that rats can fit into holes as small as a quarter, so if you've got any gaps around your shed, they'll be sure to find a way in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rats don't hibernate during the winter months, instead they desperately seek out warm shelter. And while there's one thing you should clear from your yard to prevent rats, you should also be focused on your shed.

Sources indicate that it's the perfect spot for rats to take up residence and once they find somewhere they like, they'll stick around and populate. So, before you end up with a rat infestation in your shed, here's the 3 things I recommend doing every winter to make sure they stay out (and stay away from your home, too).

Recent findings suggest that rats can fit into holes as small as a quarter, so if you've got any gaps around your shed, they'll be sure to find a way in. And if they don't find an appropriate hole, they might chew one of their own to gain access. So, what I like to do every winter is a thorough check of the exterior and interior of my shed looking for any holes.

If you find any, it also matters what you seal the gap with, as they may just break their way through something too flimsy.

In a recent development, for this, I recommend using a steel wool or wire mesh. If you notice they're digging underneath, it might also be worth laying some concrete slabs or gravel around these areas, too.

Steel wool is great for filling holes and blocking gaps around your shed. Then, the rats won't be able to chew through, creating the perfect barrier to keep them out. It can be used for both indoor and outdoor filling and can be easily cut to size with scissors. With this 2-Pack, you'll get 3" x 10ft coverage.

The problem with rats moving into your shed is that once they're there, you'll likely need to call in pest control to get them out. If you try and deal with it yourself by going in and moving things around, you might encourage the rats to move towards your home and into your garden instead.

To prevent this, I like to give my shed a good sort out before winter to make sure there's no places for the rats to hide.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

I like to grab a few plastic boxes with lids to store anything in that I might have been leaving discarded on the floor and, if you've got space, shelves are also great for moving things off the floor and keeping them away from gnawing teeth.

According to recent reports, while storing any seeds, bulbs or bird food in your shed seems like a good idea, it's not so true in winter. As well as looking for shelter, rats are also looking for food. So, if you have seeds and a shed, they'll more than happily move in.

Recent findings suggest that what I like to do is move all the seeds and anything else the rats might want to eat out of my shed and seal them away inside my home instead. But, if you don't have room, putting these things into stainless steel containers with screw-on lids and leaving them in your shed will keep them away from rats.

Industry observers note that with these three simple steps, I've avoided rats year-in-year-out and, hopefully, you will too. Fortunately, doing these tasks is also super affordable and will cost you far less to carry out than calling in pest control.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh York City is no stranger to bad weather, be it blazing-hot summers, snow-packed winters, or fierce windstorms. Unfortunately for countless families who have made it a holiday tradition to turn on the TV and watch giant totems of pop culture sail in the streets of the great city, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially delayed due to a forecast of rain and windstorms--a first in its 100-year history. In recent years, gaming icons have become more and more prominent during the parade. Beginning in 1993, a balloon of Sonic the Hedgehog marked the first game character to float among the procession. Since then, more characters have joined the festivities, including Mario, Pac-Man, Pikachu, and even Red the Angry Bird, among others. However, those who have followed the history of Macy's balloons know that the mix of bad weather and massive, floating objects can result in genuine danger for balloon handlers, bystanders, and objects on the streets. Rather infamously, Sonic's 1993 appearance was marred by an incident where the balloon got stuck on a lamppost, popping the balloon and injuring two bystanders. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmTC0m7wQbs Other balloon bursts have proved even more catastrophic, with a series of mishaps in 1997 leading to a Cat in the Hat balloon causing injuries that left a woman comatose for days. Since then, more emphasis has rightfully been put on safety. While it might be disappointing to not be able to point at the TV and go "Mario!" with your younger cousins around the TV tomorrow, the balloons will get a chance to fly on Saturday starting at 8:30 AM ET, when the weather is likely to be significantly less awful. You can find other ways to fill the time--but maybe ask your relatives first if it's okay to let the kiddos watch you play GTA 6. Image credit: Getty Images / Craig T Fruchtman.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that some people collect works of art; others collect clothes. When I heard about a Parisian who had amassed thousands of Ralph Lauren pieces, my curiosity got the better of me and I wanted to learn more. Séverin Naudet, a former digital adviser to François Fillon when he was France’s prime minister, lives on the fifth floor of a beautiful Haussmann-style building. The tall, dark-haired 50-year-old appears not to age. Since leaving his role with the government in 2012, he has started a digital marketing company and is now also exploring opportunities in luxury and wellness.

At his home, he displays part of his wardrobe, and I realize that the rumors about Naudet are true. He shows me dozens of pairs of sneakers, tuxedo jackets and velvet shoes, pants and shirts, more jackets, and then there are also mugs, books, and pillows. In the bedroom, the linens bear the American designer’s label, while tableware from Ralph Lauren’s Burleigh Collection, carefully wrapped up and placed in a Carrefour bag, is ready to be taken to his house in Brittany, where “more sailboat-inspired” pieces are stored. There are also sorbet-colored swimsuits piled on the plump armrests of a club chair. “About 20 years ago I donated all my other clothes to a charity. Since then, I’ve worn nothing but Ralph Lauren,” he explains, barefoot and dressed in jeans and a Polo shirt, next to a jacket from Denim & Supply, a Ralph Lauren brand that existed from 2011 to 2016 and is now coveted by collectors. Naudet’s Ralph Lauren pieces represent more than just a wardrobe; they embody a way of life that embraces every facet of the American brand founded in 1967—from preppy cool to sophisticated, Gatsby-style chic, and including many nautical pieces that connect to another of Naudet’s passions: sailing.

A selection from his collection of sneakers and dress shoes.

In a recent development, but how does one fall in love with a brand to the point of making it part of every facet of their life? “As a teenager, I had body image complications. I had bowlegs, and I didn’t feel comfortable in my own skin,” he explains. Walking into a Double RL store changed everything: “I tried on a pair of Low Straight jeans and it was magical—they were perfectly cut, elegant, and stylish. I almost felt sexy. I had straight legs and a nice butt,” he notes with a laugh.

It has been revealed that his connection to the American brand speaks volumes about that magic formula that is the goal of retailers around the world: combining storytelling with emotional attachment. “Polo was the cure for a certain melancholy that was the result of a gloomy childhood. Ralph Lauren instilled in me a spirit of joy, where yellows, pinks, and sky blues, stripes and madras fabrics, evoke summer, the sea, and sailing,” explains the man who has amassed several thousand Ralph Lauren items.

As retail experiences increasingly take place online, there’s nothing Naudet loves more than going to a physical store. Walking into one is like stepping into “the family home I never had,” he explains. “A Ralph Lauren flagship store can feel like visiting a house in the Hamptons, a Parisian hotel for a perfect Christmas, or a Newly introduced York apartment with a view of Central Park.” Ralph Lauren locations are must-visits on the entrepreneur’s itineraries. In Manhattan, he always visits the West Broadway store. He knows, of course, the ones in London and Los Angeles, as well as Manda in Brussels, where he goes in search of vintage pieces. His favorite store, however, remains the one in the mansion on Boulevard Saint-Germain in Paris, where every year he celebrates Christmas at its Ralph’s restaurant.

One might call him a “perfectionist,” but he prefers “meticulous.” He will go to lengths to repair clothes, even if it requires tracking down the original fabrics or finding an expert to repair braided leather straps. He’s also interested in the story behind the brand and how design choices and corporate strategies have made it what it is today. “Ralph Lauren is a marketing genius, and his advertising is never simply advertising. He works instead like a filmmaker; he tells a story. All you need is an image, even without a product. He created a family that we all dream of being a part of by, for example, choosing his wife, Ricky, as his muse. Their marriage has lasted 60 years!” the former adviser shares. And at a time when the world is wondering and worrying about the future, Ralph Lauren and his mythologies are calm and soothing: “In a daily life saturated with screens, images, and now artificial intelligence, Ralph Lauren continues to offer a world that is profoundly real, tactile, and inhabited.” The proof? In a fashion world sometimes tinged with gloom, Ralph Lauren posted a 15% increase in revenue for 2025, surpassing $8 billion for the first time. And in the first quarter of 2026, growth continued strong at 14%.

He quotes from memory Tocqueville’s description of Fresh England in 1835 as “a region left to the dreams of the imagination, which one ought to abandon to the free trials of innovators.” Ralph Lauren is, for Naudet, the brand that stands above the fray, its founder a dreamer embodying “the finest qualities of the United States, from Tocqueville to the present day.” We ask if, as the ultimate embodiment of the American dream, Ralph Lauren, 86, would make a good president? Naudet, an expert on the inner workings of power, smiles: “He possesses at least three key qualities needed to be a good president: He understands the times, he has broad appeal, and he inspires people to dream. The rest is part of the mystery of democracy, and America is a great democracy.”.

Recent findings suggest that if the self-made Latest Yorker has ever wondered who his biggest fan in France is, Vanity Fair has found him. Before our conversation ends, Naudet tells me that recently, as he does every year around this time, he bought two pairs of Heritage Straight jeans, and also spotted a leather jacket lined with shearling that he wanted. It’s “admittedly a bit pricey,” but he’s certain it’ll be perfect once the temperatures drop.

This story was originally published in Vanity Fair France.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game. Anyone looking to externalize their inner animal spirit is in danger of being hunted, and you'll find out for yourself just how much the fictional state of Leonida hates Furries when you're given the chance to save one of them from being murdered by the cops. Should you help them? Absolutely, if you want an easy payday or a new weapon for your arsenal. How to find Chase the Fox Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly. The mission takes place after Chapter 3, on Miramar Drive in Crosstown, Vice City, and you'll want to be cruising around that area at night, between midnight and 4 AM. Once it starts, you'll see cops pull up to hunt down a Furry by the name of Chase, and if you drive up to him, you can either give him a lift or leave him to his brutal fate. Outrun the cops If you do choose to help Chase, then get ready to be hunted down by cops. You'll pick up a three-star Wanted level, which means the cops will be in mildly hot pursuit of your vehicle. Reach the parking garage Chase will direct you to a nearby parking garage, where his Furry allies are waiting. After a short standoff, they'll welcome you into their ranks as an honorary Furry. Courier the group to safety To get the law off your polyester tail, one of your new allies will take your car and use it to distract the cops. Get inside the van, and you can bring the other Furries home to their swanky pad in Starfish Island. While you're driving, the Furries will interact with each other, and you can watch their hijinks. Choose your reward Once Chase and his pals are back home, you'll be offered one of two rewards: $15,000 in cash or the unique Furry DW-9 submachine gun. Personally, I'd go with the gun since it's easy enough to make cash in GTA 6, and having more weapons is never a bad idea. You'll also gain safehouse access to the Furry group's hideout, where you can stock up on weapons and body armor. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday deals start showing up long before Black Friday actually arrives, and it's easy to shop most sales online without ever having to set foot in a store.
  • Sources indicate that the first 100 shoppers in line at Target on Black Friday will receive a gift card worth $25, $50, or $100, and one shopper at every store will get a $1,000 gift card.
  • The first 200 shoppers at every Kohl's store on Black Friday will get a voucher for Kohl's Cash worth $5 to $100.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday deals start showing up long before Black Friday actually arrives, and it's easy to shop most sales online without ever having to set foot in a store. But if you are willing to go early, stand in line, and navigate the crowds, you may be able to get some free stuff for your effort. Here are the freebies on offer this Black Friday.

Sources indicate that the first 100 shoppers in line at Target on Black Friday will receive a gift card worth $25, $50, or $100, and one shopper at every store will get a $1,000 gift card. Stores open at 6 a.m., and tickets redeemable for free gift cards will be handed out starting approximately an hour before. Shoppers must exchange their tickets for their gift card within the first hour after doors open.

The first 200 shoppers at every Kohl's store on Black Friday will get a voucher for Kohl's Cash worth $5 to $100. Doors open at 5 a.m. If you show up on Saturday, Nov. 28 instead, you're eligible for a Sephora at Kohl's coupon (also worth $5 to $100).

Industry observers note that if you're a MyLowe's Rewards member and you show up early on Black Friday, you could get one of several free buckets filled with products and coupons. The first 50 loyalty program members in line will receive a Black Friday Mystery Bucket, and four of those individuals will win one of the following grand prizes:.

A major appliance (under $2,000).

The next 100 members get a Golden Mini Bucket, which contains $5 in MyLowe's Monday and a 20% off coupon, among other things. The loyalty program is free to join, and doors open at 6 a.m.

The first 250 shoppers at Bass Pro Shops and Cabela's locations on Black Friday will receive a promo card worth between $10 and $500. The cards are valid Dec. 4 through 26, so you can't use them to shop that day.

According to recent reports, JCPenney is running scheduled giveaways in stores throughout the day on Black Friday, so you could get free products even if you aren't there when doors open. If you line up at 5 a.m., you will get a peel-away card that is good for $10 off, $50 off, or $500 off your purchase, as well as a free Harry Potter mini snow globe. Additional giveaways will take place at 9 a.m., 1 p.m., and 5 p.m. for those in line.

Michaels is giving away 500 Countdown to Craftsmas advent calendars in stores on Black Friday while supplies last. The calendars come with store coupons, and some include other freebies and cash prizes up to a $100 gift card. One winner will receive a $10,000 nationwide grand prize.

Academy Sports is distributing bonus cards worth $20, $50, or $100 to the first 100 customers in line on Black Friday between 5 a.m. and 6 a.m. CT. Prize amounts will be randomly awarded among entrants. Academy Sports has locations across more than 20 states.

Industry observers note that best Buy's Black Friday promo isn't strictly free, but members of the My Best Buy rewards program (including the free tier) can purchase a $100 gift card for $60. There is a limit of one per person while supplies last, and cards can be used immediately, so you can take advantage of sales.

The first 30 shoppers at Golf Galaxy locations on Black Friday are eligible for instant prizes, including products, gift cards, and in-store services. One person per location will win a swag bag worth more than $500. Doors open at 7 a.m.

Sources indicate that if you're among the first 500 shoppers at Fleet Farm when doors open at 5 a.m. on Black Friday, you'll receive a plush eagle toy. The organization has also been running an "Orange Friday" event with in-store giveaways, though these have passed at most locations.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Recent findings suggest that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the new one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The company has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings.

If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms.

In a recent development, this week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred. The welcome pack for Firestone is valued at $100, and it includes an exclusive Talia skin, chests, avatars and gems. Newly introduced players must reach stage 15 to claim it.

Next week, you can get Strange Antiquities for free. Run a shop full of occult antiques in the eerie town of Undermere, uncover sinister secrets, help the locals out, and do pet your adorable shop cat.

We're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic users have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Following our extensive roster of physical media and books for movie and TV fans, we're wrapping up the 2026 /Film Holiday Gift Guide by taking a look at a bunch of toys, collectibles, and games pulling from the latest and most beloved films and TV demonstrates.
  • Are you in the market for some cool action figures from Marvel and DC movies?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Following our extensive roster of physical media and books for movie and TV fans, we're wrapping up the 2026 /Film Holiday Gift Guide by taking a look at a bunch of toys, collectibles, and games pulling from the latest and most beloved films and TV demonstrates.

Are you in the market for some cool action figures from Marvel and DC movies? Do you want some throwback toys from the likes of the "Star Wars," "Masters of the Universe," "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles" and "Transformers" franchises? Are you still collecting Funko POPs? Do you need detailed figures of The Muppets? Are your kids still desperate for "KPop Demon Hunters" toys? Maybe it's time to get building with some incredible LEGO sets.

If action figures and collectibles aren't your thing, you may enjoy spending some time putting together some substantial puzzles from Theory 11, or logging into the latest video games based on movies and TV reveals.

Speaking of games, let's kick things off with a fun latest holiday movie themed game called We Pitch You a Movie Christmas. Using cards with actors and story ideas, players go head-to-head pitching a wild new Christmas movie, and everyone else decides which one sounds the best. But there are other ways to play too!

The Thanksgiving holiday is allowing Brooke Hogan to reflect on the loss of her father, wrestling icon Hulk Hogan.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve realized that so much of my grief exists in what we will miss together, rather than even what we’ve lost…,” Brooke, 38, wrote via Instagram on Wednesday, November 25. “It’s a strange thing. Nostalgia in reverse. Longing for moments somewhere in the future that feel almost as familiar as memories.”.

The founder of BB Designs by Brooke continued, “I miss him in the thought of him falling asleep on my couch, after too much pecan pie, surrounded by the beautiful little family that is an extension of his own. I imagine the evolution of our relationship as I grow older.”.

Recent findings suggest that hulk died in July 2025 at the age of 71. His cause of death was acute myocardial infarction, most commonly known as a heart attack, according to documents obtained by Us.

Although her relationship with Hulk was complicated, Brooke — who shared a throwback photo with her father for her latest post — has been open about her grieving journey and processing different emotions.

“Sometimes the circumstances surrounding a relationship don’t accurately reflect the love that exists within it,” she wrote. “Life and dishonest influence can create distance between two hearts that were never meant to be far apart. I’ll die on that hill. No daughter doesn’t want her daddy.”.

“How strange it is to miss someone in a place you’ve yet to visit, at an age you’ve yet to reach, in a moment that’s still somewhere in your future,” she added.

According to recent reports, married to Steven Oleksy, Brooke has two children and currently lives in Florida. She continues to have a fractured relationship with her mom, Linda, 67, and brother, Nick, 36.

Check our latest news in Google News.

Check our latest news in Apple News.

In a recent development, “Grief stretches in both directions. It lives in the memories behind you, but also in the life unfolding ahead of you,” Brooke wrote in her latest post. “There’s an entirely different dimension of grief that exists within the beauty of living. The more life there is to celebrate, the more places there are to miss someone.”.

While Brooke acknowledged that she has “so much life ahead of me,” it could be why she feels her dad’s absence “so deeply.”.

“I’ll miss him in chapters of my life that haven’t even been written yet,” she said. “It’s a longing born entirely out of so much love with nowhere to go. It’s nostalgia in reverse. Being homesick for a future with someone you needed and loved the most.”.

  • Industry observers note that roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6's record-breaking launch, and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions. Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB mentioned it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVyCl_Euhmo The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers. With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

Cheat codes have long been a part of the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise, and the tradition continues with GTA 6. Not only does GTA 6 support cheats, but it also has a menu that lists all of them as well as instructions for unlocking them. However, you cannot fire up the game and start using cheats from the beginning. In fact, it requires quite a bit of work on your part. Here's how to unlock cheat codes in GTA 6, how to see the list of cheats, as well as the 10 best cheat codes in GTA 6.

According to recent reports, gone are the good old days when you could fire up GTA, enable god mode, unlimited ammo, no reload, spawn a jetpack, and run around the entire city destroying things at will. In GTA 6, you'll need to complete the main story to unlock the ability to use cheat codes. On top of that, you'll have to complete challenges of various difficulty levels to access specific cheat codes. Some of these cheats unlock the moment you finish the main story. Others, however, are quite challenging or time-consuming. For instance, unlimited reload requires you to win 25 gold medals at shooting ranges.

Once you complete the main story in GTA 6, just go to in-game settings, and you'll see a newly introduced Cheats tab. This lists all 61 cheats and how to unlock them. You'll see the actual button combo for each cheat right after you complete the unlock requirement.

Unfortunately, there are some serious gameplay ramifications to using cheat codes in GTA 6. For starters, you can't save the game once you input even one cheat code. That's why it's best to save before you start using cheats, to avoid losing progress. Using cheat codes will also disable trophies and achievements in GTA 6.

To start using cheat codes in GTA 6, you'll have to get your character to pull up the smartphone by pressing the up arrow on the D-Pad. Then, hold L1+R1, and press the cheat's key combination on the D-Pad.

While there are a lot of cheat codes in GTA 6, these are 10 of the best, listed with the right key combination, and the condition to unlock them:.

To stop needing reloads, you need to win 25 gold medals at shooting ranges in GTA 6. The key combination is: down, up, right, down, left, left, up, down, down, up.

According to recent reports, if you complete 100 workouts during your GTA 6 playthrough, you'll unlock the cheat that lets you instantly obtain body armor. Press this key combination to make it work: down, up, left, up, up, up, up, up, down, down.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The geography of Earth in the Marvel Cinematic Universe is mostly similar to our own world, but it does have a few fictional countries thrown in, including Wakanda, Sokovia, and now Latveria. The home nation of Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.), Latveria is sandwiched between Romania, Hungary, and Serbia in Marvel's comics, but it's generally just sort of vaguely Eastern European. That means that the role of Doctor Doom in "Avengers: Doomsday" called for a vaguely Eastern European accent.

It has been revealed that based on what we've heard from the film's trailers so far, especially this fresh international teaser for "Avengers: Doomsday," Downey certainly seems to have delivered on the "vague" part. In this latest promo, Doom issues a warning that "You shall all kneel before Doom," while also conveniently acting as a bit of a hype man by name-checking some of the big superhero teams that will appear in the movie. (The Thunderbolts are missing from the list, though, possibly because Doom was confused by their branding).

New international teaser for 'AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY'.

According to recent reports, in theaters December 18. pic.twitter.com/wTudC8pKc9.

— Avengers Updates (@AvengersUpdated) November 24, 2026.

Industry observers note that downey's Doom accent has been widely compared to the voice of ancient vampire Nandor the Relentless (Kayvan Novak) in the TV show "What We Do in the Shadows." (Nandor is also from a fictional country, Al Qolnidar.) However, in this particular teaser it's more reminiscent of eccentric German filmmaker Werner Herzog. Even Downey himself has said that he struggled to settle on an accent.

"Part of me didn't want to go Eastern European," Robert Downey Jr. explained, regarding Doctor Doom's accent, in an interview with Empire. "I had written this manifesto speech that [Doom] makes, and I laid down this voice note of him addressing his people, and I started to find it there.".

Downey already appeared in 10 Marvel Cinematic Universe movies as Tony Stark, aka Iron Man, so Doom presented a fresh challenge for him: "I don't want to say Tony's like rolling off a log, but I know that swing pattern." Comparatively, the process of figuring out Doom, from superficialities like his accent to his deeper motivations, was "painstaking." The fact that the character spends most of his time — possibly the entire movie, if you believe Downey's co-star Chris Evans — wearing a full face mask presented another challenge. "Honestly, a lot of it was just the eyes," Downey told Empire, adding, "I ain't gonna lie to you. A lot of this we were just trying to figure it out ... It was a bit of an exploration.".

Recent findings suggest that the question of whether or not Doom will take his mask off is a major one, as Downey's face is pretty recognizable within the world of the MCU. For now, though, much about Doom is still shrouded in mystery. Fans will have to wait until "Avengers: Doomsday" releases on December 18, 2026, to see (and hear) more from this classic Marvel villain.

#131635. What’s Real and What’s Not in Netflix’s ‘The Altruists’

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1144 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vanityfair ↗ Open Full Page

What’s Real and What’s Not in Netflix’s ‘The Altruists’

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1144 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that even if you followed the news closely in the early 2020s, the sheer audacity of the fraud committed by Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison—as dramatized in Netflix’s new limited series The Altruists, starring Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner—will shock you anew.
  • Recent findings suggest that I found the series to be especially striking in the context of last week’s historic Anthropic IPO, which ironically fell on the same day as the premiere.
  • The Altruists also depicts a surprisingly tender romance between two socially inept, possibly sociopathic adrenaline junkies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that even if you followed the news closely in the early 2020s, the sheer audacity of the fraud committed by Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison—as dramatized in Netflix’s new limited series The Altruists, starring Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner—will shock you anew. The show, which follows the stunning multibillion-dollar collapse of the crypto exchange FTX, starts off a bit slow, but accelerates episode by episode until its high-octane finale.

Recent findings suggest that I found the series to be especially striking in the context of last week’s historic Anthropic IPO, which ironically fell on the same day as the premiere. Some of that company’s founders and employees share similar intellectual roots to The Altruist’s protagonists; watching its fictionalized Caroline Ellison, in particular, justify astoundingly reckless behavior with her system of mathematical-optimization-of-everything felt uncannily like watching frontier labs proceed with a seemingly inexplicable appetite for risk.

The Altruists also depicts a surprisingly tender romance between two socially inept, possibly sociopathic adrenaline junkies. (According to people involved with the project, the working title for the project was Untitled Love Story.) But as with any fictionalized account, the series takes some liberties with the characters and plot. If you’re anything like me, you want to know what exactly is fact, and what is fiction.

I spoke with Kevin T. Dugan and Jen Wieczner, two of the reporters who exposed the FTX fiasco in real time, and who consulted on the series. “When Jen and I started working with Graham Moore, the showrunner, he made it really clear that he wanted this to be very character driven. Nobody wants an eight-hour lecture on how the blockchain works,” Dugan tells me.

“The bones of the show are rooted in reality,” says Wieczner. Understanding these flawed and complicated characters helps explain “how one decision leads to another decision and a small oopsies turns into a multibillion-dollar fraud and this huge criminal conspiracy.”.

Even if there’s a little fiction in the nitty-gritty, Dugan says that there is one overarching truth he hopes the series will reveal: “That even the prettiest ideas still have to turn into reality through imperfect people, and those imperfect people will end up making mistakes that they cannot foresee.” Here’s what the show ripped from real life—and where it took some creative license.

CAROLINE ELLISON WROTE SEXY HARRY POTTER FAN FICTION.

Not quite. In the first episode, Caroline is humiliated when her raunchy writing titled “A Ride on Draco’s Nimbus” surfaces online. And while it’s true that Ellison was a huge Harry Potter fan, there is no evidence she wrote erotic fan fiction herself. Instead, this plot point is likely gesturing toward Ellison’s 2010s-era Tumblr, which was called WorldOptimisation—a reference to a 660,000-word-long work of Harry Potter fan fiction by Silicon Valley philosopher Eliezer Yudkowsky. Yudkowsky’s work popularized the kind of mathematically strategic thinking Ellison applies to love and business alike.

SAM TRABUCCO’S “INFINITE MONEY HACK”.

In episode six, Sam Trabucco (played by Alex Lawther) makes the mistake of introducing Sam and Caroline to a hack that proves irresistible: FTX can mint its own coin, FTT, and then allow its crypto trading firm, Alameda, to take out large loans using off-market FTT as collateral. Alameda can then use those loans to place highly leveraged, incredibly risky bets on FTX—which in turn increases the value of FTT. (TL;DR: it’s a perfect loop.) Appalling as it sounds, in real life, this practice is more or less exactly what brought SBF’s empire tumbling down.

“One of the things that led to the FTX bank run,” explains Wieczner, “was the leaked balance sheet that demonstrated that much of FTX and Alameda’s holdings were in FTT, which was FTX’s own coin. So that if that went to zero, it was like a house of cards and things just would’ve fallen apart. And that’s why you see at the end why is everything is falling…you have that kind of death spiral effect.”.

As for Trabucco, he and his yacht (yes, it was really named Soak My Deck) didn’t get off unscathed. Trabucco didn’t face criminal charges, but was forced to liquidate many of his assets in order to help return about $80 million to defrauded investors.

CAROLINE ELLISON WAS INTO POLYAMORY.

True. Caroline chronicled some of her adventures in nonmonogamy on her since-deleted Tumblr. She once wrote, “The only acceptable style of poly is best characterized as something like ‘imperial Chinese harem.’”.

Real! In the final episode of the series, SBF presents a last-ditch blueprint: He wants to repurpose his early stake in Anthropic to cover the losses of billions of dollars in customer funds. Indeed, FTX did use $500 million in customer funds to purchase a 13.5% stake in Anthropic’s Series B in late 2021. Of course, Sam’s plan did not pass muster. Yet if it had, he’d have been in the clear. After the company’s IPO last week, Alameda’s stake would be worth about $35 billion, according to The New York Times—enough to solve the disgraced firm’s liquidity issues several times over. Oh well.

CAROLINE ELLISON CONFESSED IN FRONT OF HER STAFF.

True. In the penultimate episode, a visibly cracking Caroline delivers a halting confession amidst fits of nervous giggles to a shocked staff, telling them that she knew about FTX’s shortfall of user funds that would add up to more than $8 billion. I was sure this scene had been invented, but lo and behold: Ellison did admit that she had been aware of the inappropriate transfers between the two firms at a December 2022 all-staff meeting. You can even listen to the leaked recording online.

CAROLINE ELLISON BEARS MORE RESPONSIBILITY THAN SBF.

Recent findings suggest that I felt the show tilted towards placing the blame on Ellison, who is portrayed as incorrigibly risk-addicted and the muse behind SBF’s worst decisions. Constance Wang, who is played in the series by Madison Hu, is just one of the former FTX employees who found the show misrepresentative. In a lengthy X post, she rebutted its narrative: Ellison, remarked Hu, “wasn’t nearly that reckless, and she was never the one pushing to go all in. In a recent development, "Avengers: Doomsday" may feel like the grandaddy of all Marvel Cinematic Universe films, but even this gargantuan production can't hold a candle to the absolute icon at its heart. The legendary Patrick Stewart left us in October of 2026, and his loss will continue to be keenly felt among family, friends, and fans for years to come. The fact that he agreed to return to the Marvel franchise and reprise his role as Charles Xavier already lent tremendous weight to the story. But now, knowing that his final day on the set of "Doomsday" was also his last on any film, moviegoers will end up bringing mountains of emotional baggage with them on opening weekend.

According to recent reports, in a new profile with Entertainment Weekly, the cast and crew of "Doomsday" opened up about their memories of working with Stewart, the immense legacy he leaves behind, and the unforgettable experience they had watching him on his very last day filming. To Kevin Feige, the Marvel head who was present as a lowly associate producer during Stewart's very first appearance as the mutant leader in 2000's "X-Men," the words Stewart spoke after wrapping filming on "Doomsday" feel even more poignant in retrospect:.

Industry observers note that "He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew. We didn't know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.".

Co-director Anthony Russo noted that, "It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew." Stewart passed away from Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, so it must've taken a Herculean effort for him to show up and perform each day.

Sources indicate that despite Patrick Stewart's irreplaceable loss, it does feel like a gift that we'll be able to enjoy one last performance of his in the weeks ahead. In fact, according to "Avengers: Doomsday" co-director Joe Russo, Charles Xavier's journey in the film will feel like a poignant echo of Stewart's celebrated life:.

Sources indicate that "In a lot of ways, Xavier's the conscience in the movie. He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who's his best friend, in the film. It's a very emotional scene about forgiveness and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.".

It has been revealed that after watching both Xavier and McKellen as Magneto butt heads, debate each other, and play peaceful games of chess across several "X-Men" movies, it'll undoubtedly be a treat to watch them do so one more time (all the more so given Stewart and McKellen's real-life friendship). For his part, Kevin Feige acknowledged that he and the Russo brothers have been busy putting the final touches on "Doomsday" — including a tribute in memory of Stewart, likely in the end credits of the film. As he put it:.

Sources indicate that "We're long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us. We're looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.".

Industry observers note that considering similar memorials for dearly-departed figures like Leonard Nimoy, Carrie Fisher, Chadwick Boseman, and many more in recent years, don't expect a single dry eye in the house once the lights come on. "Avengers: Doomsday" will arrive in theaters on December 18, 2026.

  • Industry observers note that tarantino didn't direct "Cliff Booth" — he handed those duties over to David Fincher.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" follow.

According to recent reports, forget the MCU. Real ones know that Quentin Tarantino has been building his own cinematic universe for years. For instance: while this is never officially stated by anyone on screen, Michael Madsen's character from "Reservoir Dogs" is supposed to be the brother of John Travolta's character from "Pulp Fiction" (there was even a plan for a crossover movie, but it never happened). Beyond character connections, Tarantino also likes to drop his own fictional products into his films, and "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" keeps this trend going.

Industry observers note that tarantino didn't direct "Cliff Booth" — he handed those duties over to David Fincher. But Tarantino still wrote the script, and Fincher keeps the Easter eggs intact. The biggest example: Major Kahuna Burger. Early in the film, we see Brad Pitt's Cliff Booth pick up some food at Big Kahuna Burger to bring home to his dad, Gus (Peter Weller). Tarantino fans will, of course, recognize that burger joint: it was prominently mentioned in "Pulp Fiction," and we see Samuel L. Jackson's character Jules take a big bite of a burger while intimidating some crooks who are about to meet a violent end.

Recent findings suggest that but wait, there's more! Another Tarantino product that highlights up in "The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" are the famous Red Apple Cigarettes. Red Apples have been mentioned in virtually every Tarantino film, and they were even a part of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," the film that "Cliff Booth" serves as a sequel to.

In "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," Leonardo DiCaprio's Rick Dalton filmed a commercial for Red Apple Cigarettes (believe it or not, kids, there used to be commercials for cigarettes on TV). "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" keeps the tradition alive while also giving us a nice little callback. During one scene, we see Cliff watching a newly introduced Red Apple commercial on TV. And who is starring in that commercial? None other than Sharon Tate, played by Margot Robbie in a cameo.

"Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" ended by literally changing history, and allowing Sharon Tate and her friends to completely avoid their tragic murders at the hands of the Manson family. "Cliff Booth" confirms that since Sharon is still alive in 1977, when the film is set, she's still out there acting, too.

I Love The Emperor's New Groove, But David Spade Has Some Blunt Thoughts About Disney

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Emperor’s New Groove is one of those Walt Disney Animation movies that will forever and always be imprinted in my brain.
  • According to recent reports, the animation movie landscape has changed a lot over the years.
  • I was the last guy to do a Disney movie where they remarked it was ‘an honor’, and that’s why I didn’t get a lot of money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Emperor’s New Groove is one of those Walt Disney Animation movies that will forever and always be imprinted in my brain. The 2000 film came out at just the right time in my childhood when I’d put it on repeat. I could honestly quote most of it front to back. However, I had no idea about the experience Kuzco's voice actor, David Spade, had.

According to recent reports, the animation movie landscape has changed a lot over the years. These days all the big roles go to Hollywood names rather than talents known specifically for voice acting. David Spade, who famously got his start on SNL, spoke to this while talking about The Emperor’s Fresh Groove with these words:.

I was the last guy to do a Disney movie where they remarked it was ‘an honor’, and that’s why I didn’t get a lot of money. And then, they came out with Shrek, and everyone got $5 million bucks, and I go 'Wait, what the fuck is going on?'.

Hey, he makes a good point. Prior to the 21st Century, animated movies weren't paying substantial-name celebrities the big bucks. David Spade was also working with Disney Animation at a time when the studio wasn’t making blockbusters to the degree it is now with the likes of Frozen or Moana. Spade even disclosed how much he made, saying this:.

I got $75,000, which sounds like a lot. It was a lot… They rat fucked me.

Shrek came out in 2001 – one year after The Emperor’s New Groove – and made almost half a billion worldwide. It helped usher in an era of blockbuster animated films led by A-list celebrities that we continue to live in. The Emperor's New Groove made $169 million worldwide, and was actually thought of as a commercial flop at the time of its release.

Spade’s comments about The Emperor’s New Groove were made while on his podcast Fly On The Wall with guest Denis Leary, who famously plays Diego the saber-tooth tiger in the Ice Age movies. Ice Age came out a couple of years after Spade’s Disney movie, and has a sixth installment among upcoming Disney movies in 2027. Leary mentioned he and the rest of the Ice Age cast have received pay bumps since first signing up to the franchise because they are watched so frequently on streaming.

According to recent reports, even though I imagine it’s a bummer that Spade lost out on some cash he might have gotten for the same amount of work a couple of years later on something else, he also made a point of saying he loves The Emperor’s New Groove and how well it turned out. But he did so while pointing out something else about being a voice actor on a Disney film that was hard to deal with in the moment….

Industry observers note that no, I did it and it just kept going and going, and I’m like, ‘Guys, I don’t want to drive out to Disney every day and just lay down an hour or two of tracks. I’m like Denis Leary, I have shit to do on my day off. I love the movie now, but during it I was starting to get a little itchy. Like, there’s no ending. I really love it, and they’re miracle workers with the freaking animation.

Recent findings suggest that animated movies like The Emperor’s New Groove famously go through a long production process. The 2000 movie in particular did so because it was actually originally an entirely different movie called Kingdom of the Sun. It was more inspired by The Prince and the Pauper, featured Owen Wilson in a voice role, and Spade was playing a character named Manco instead of Kuzco before they shifted directions. No wonder he was getting antsy while making it!

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

While I can understand David Spade’s blunt thoughts about working with Disney, I’m so happy he stuck it out and played Kuzco. The movie has brought me so much joy throughout my life, and it’s certainly one of the most beloved projects of his career. You can watch it now with a Disney+ subscription.

He would have focused on a pair of beloved characters, specifically the best droids in the "Star Wars" property.

On a recent episode of the "Happy Sad Confused" podcast, Fincher revealed that he had a conversation with former Lucasfilm President Kathleen Kennedy about taking th studio public before Disney bought Lucasfilm in 2012. But what would Fincher have done with "Star Wars" had that panned out? Perhaps not what you'd expect.

In a recent development, his interest lay with C-3PO and R2-D2, primarily. Not Luke Skywalker. Not Princess Leia. A protocol droid and his astromech companion. And while Fincher admitted he didn't have a full pitch, he did have a rough idea. Here's what he had to say:.

"I said, 'The thing that has always interested me about — certainly from the first movie — was the relationship between [C-]3PO and R2[-D2]. That they were essentially slaves who would bear witness to the folly of man. I always thought that, them being captured by Jawas, and then sold off and being on the periphery and witnessing the Skywalker Saga, was such a crucial element to it. [...] There was a kind of moral judgment. It was fairly obvious even from 3PO [...] he had a kind of understanding as to what the Empire meant, how evil they were.".

"He was kind of trying to decide whether or not he wanted to invest in having a relationship with Luke Skywalker when he's getting his oil bath [in 'A New Hope'], and they're talking," Fincher added.

"Even from ['The Empire Strikes Back'], when 3PO is turned back on, and he recounts for you what he sees with the stormtroopers already being in [...] Bespin," David FIncher continued. "Whenever they used the robots for that, I was always really excited. I always thought that was kind of interesting, that you have to go through the recorder, like the court reporter, to find out what it is that happened.".

Sources indicate that notably, C-3PO actor Anthony Daniels is the only actor to appear in all nine main "Star Wars" movies, while Kenny Baker portrayed R2-D2 in the original trilogy. These are characters who certainly have earned time in the spotlight, but using them as the crux of a upcoming era for the franchise? That's a strange idea.

Be that as it may, Fincher and Kathleen Kennedy were interested in seeing if they could make something happen. Fincher, however, revealed that Disney's purchase of Lucasfilm (a deal that encompassed $4 billion in cash and stocks) nixed those aims. As the filmmaker recalled:.

"I stated to [Kennedy], I kind of pitched her this idea, I said, 'Let's take this thing to Wall Street and let the market decide.' And I think it was a month later or something, she said, 'Bad news. Apparently there's a $7 billion offer on the table,' and I said, 'We're not going to beat that.'".

It has been revealed that george Lucas later opened up about selling Lucafilm to Disney, describing it as "very, very painful." Of course, it proved to be enormously beneficial for Disney, financially speaking. Fincher, meanwhile, has gone on to continue enjoying a very fruitful career outside the confines of a galaxy far, far away.

  • After working at Politico, HuffPost, and The Intercept, Grim, 48, cofounded Drop Site News, an independent nonprofit news organization, in 2024, and he’s also a cohost on the antiestablishment political podcast Breaking Points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anyone still struggling to understand how Bernie Bros and MAGA voters overlap on the political Venn diagram might find answers in Ryan Grim’s audience.

Grim, a veteran journalist and self-described “leftist,” has cultivated a rather politically diverse and incongruous fan base over his two decades in journalism. On election night in Los Angeles earlier this month, a room full of socialists erupted in cheers when Grim appeared on the big screen at the Democratic Socialists of America’s watch party (Grim was a guest that night on Hasan Piker’s livestream). The next day, a friend who religiously listens to Tim Dillon, a podcaster credited with helping Trump win reelection in 2024, and Tony Hinchcliffe, a comedian who performed at a Trump rally that same year, told me that he was also a huge fan of Grim’s.

After working at Politico, HuffPost, and The Intercept, Grim, 48, cofounded Drop Site News, an independent nonprofit news organization, in 2024, and he’s also a cohost on the antiestablishment political podcast Breaking Points. He’s developed a reputation for being an equal opportunity critic of both parties, which Grim says helps explain why people all along the spectrum are attracted to his work. Even Steve Bannon (who called Grim an “intrepid reporter”) and former Republican congressman Matt Gaetz have occasionally thrown compliments his way.

“I think there’s a huge overlap with Breaking Points, Drop Site, and the whole podcast-bro world,” Grim tells Vanity Fair. “It does feel like we’ve basically become the primary news source for the podcast bros, which is not how you would have necessarily understood the world several years ago.”.

But lest anyone think that Grim has changed his views to accommodate latest fans, his frequent criticism of Israel’s war in Gaza has helped make him a target of Fox News host Mark Levin, who has called into question Drop Site’s nonprofit status.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Grim discusses his unlikely popularity among the podcast bros, why he thinks the Epstein files helped propel Democrats in 2026, why he doesn’t understand the protests against Jerry Seinfeld, and what his favorite jam band, Phish, taught him about tolerance.

This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Industry observers note that vanity Fair: You’ve talked about how being a leftist rather than a Democratic partisan has helped you build credibility with conservatives. Why is that distinction key?

Ryan Grim: [The conservatives] never thought I was a Democratic partisan, because I wasn’t. I think if you have a view of the world, people are willing to say, Okay, that’s his view of the world, and I’m going to metabolize what he’s reporting while taking into account that he has a particular view of the world.

But if you’re a partisan for Democrats or Republicans, that’s different because then you’re playing, like, strategic games with your information, and your view of whether or not something is good or bad changes with whether or not it’s good or bad for Democrats or good or bad for Republicans, rather than being grounded in some type of idea about the world.

And you’ve been criticizing Democrats for decades.

Sources indicate that yeah, I think what frustrates our critics is that they can’t be like, “Oh yeah, well, you didn’t say that when Biden was president or when Obama was president,” and it’s like, “Oh no, in fact, we mentioned this and worse,” because it didn’t matter the color of the jersey. We believed that drone strikes were wrong, or shutting down ACORN is bad, and we’re going to say it no matter who’s in office.

Recent findings suggest that jeremy [Scahill] and I have been doing this for so long that we have that track record, so I think that has really helped us build that audience across the spectrum. It’s been pretty gratifying to develop that conservative audience. It’s weird sometimes to hear a Steve Bannon or a Matt Gaetz applauding your journalism. But it’s like, hey, that doesn't necessarily mean they agree with us about our conclusions. That’s not what we’re here for. We’re here to do the reporting.

You grew up around a lot of Moral Majority conservatives in rural Maryland, and you’ve said that even though you disagreed with their politics, you didn’t necessarily think they were bad people. Is that something the left has lost sight of?

It has been revealed that they were almost universally pretty good people whose views I didn’t share as a young person and don’t now. But that’s just who they are.

I’ve talked to other people who still live in these rural areas, and they’re like, “How do I deal with these people who have these wretched beliefs?” I say, “Just deal with them as people.” They were kind of born believing that, and a lot of them are rethinking things all the time.

Industry observers note that you seem to have a lot more patience for people you disagree with than some of your fellow leftists. How do you reconcile that with your own pretty uncompromising politics?

I try to live by the creed of [left-wing political commentator] Michael Brooks. He used to say, “Be ruthless to systems, be kind to people,” and that can be very hard. But to me the most crucial thing to do is try to understand that people operate within systems, and it is the system that you’re against, not the people.

I think you’re more likely to win converts by understanding what their role is in the system and keeping your criticisms at that systemic level.

I think sometimes people go a little bit crazy. I don’t agree with Jerry Seinfeld’s politics when it comes to Israel, but I don’t understand the value of protesting Jerry Seinfeld. Maybe he’s given some money or something, but like, in general, he’s not a decision-maker. What is the upside in making him a target of protest? That part I don’t understand.

Speaking of people who disagree with you, Mark Levin has been going after Drop Site News’s nonprofit status. How seriously are you taking his efforts?

So if tomorrow Levin succeeded, and we were no longer a nonprofit, we would then carry on as a for-profit supported by our readers.

It has been revealed that I know the underlying hostility is he doesn’t like our reporting—he doesn’t want it to exist. But stripping our nonprofit status wouldn’t change that. It would just turn it into a lucrative for-profit company, which I don’t understand. Like, that’s his preferred outcome? That we make a bunch of money doing this? I don’t think it’s very well thought through.

In a recent development, but couldn’t this become a much bigger problem for journalism? There are organizations like ProPublica and The Texas Tribune that could theoretically face similar attacks.

Yes, and certainly the Trump administration has been very publicly saying that it looks to go after the entire nonprofit complex, and everybody from Sierra Club on down, because they consider them to be political enemies.

But [the Trump administration] has also gotten a lot of pushback on this from the conservative-nonprofit world, which is actually much more lucratively funded than the progressive side, because the conservatives have stated [Democrats are] going to come for organizations like The Heritage Foundation when Republicans are no longer in power.

It has been revealed that let’s talk about the midterms. Moderates saw the blue wave as a vindication of the party’s affordability-focused strategy, while progressives saw it as a mandate for a more ambitious agenda. What was your biggest takeaway?

Sources indicate that I think people are overlooking the role that the Epstein files and Trump’s cover-up, in particular, played. That was really a major break that eroded trust from his base and from independents.

Recent findings suggest that we even did a survey right after he introduced the war and asked people if they thought he was going to war with Iran to distract, at least in part, from the Epstein scandal. And by a 50-to-42 margin, the majority of the country mentioned yes, he is.

According to recent reports, whether true or not, the Epstein scandal bled into Iran, which then drove up gas prices and created all of this intense anxiety. Meanwhile, Trump is focused on the ballroom, which he’s using to collect bribes.

People believed when they elected him that he was going to drain the swamp, release the files, start no newly introduced wars, and focus instead on bringing down prices. That was what people understood he was going to do. And on all four, he just did the exact opposite, in, like, an aggressive, in-your-face, I-don’t-care-about-you kind of way.

In a recent development, you recently discussed a forensic expert’s analysis challenging the official account of Jeffrey Epstein’s death. What interested you about the coverage?

It was certainly interesting that The Upcoming York Times was willing to cover it.

Recent findings suggest that their headline was funny. The one that the Times went with said something like, “Against Conventional Wisdom,” comma, “Forensic Expert Indicates Epstein Was Murdered.” And I was like, What? What conventional wisdom are you talking about here?

I don’t think the conventional wisdom was challenged there at all.

It has been revealed that we live in this interesting world where the public can get to, like, a 70-30, 80-20 belief in something without The Latest York Times ever giving permission for that belief. And so then when they finally come around to it, like with this article, they say that the story they’re writing goes against conventional wisdom. The conventional wisdom may be wrong, but the conventional wisdom is that he was killed.

What does that say about the state of journalism?

The depressing part, from my perspective, is there’s almost nothing I can report anymore that our readers will admit they’re surprised by, and there’s pretty much nothing you could report on Epstein that would ever live up to what people just assume is true about him.

Sources indicate that all right, something considerably more fun: We’re both Phish fans, and I’ve noticed a growing MAGA contingent at their concerts. Does that bother you?

According to recent reports, well, it’s the same audience. You know, they’re just going through changes in their lives. Doesn’t frustrate me at all. All are welcome.

Sources indicate that I actually talked to Phish about this in 2002. I met the band after they played at Saturday Night Live. At the time, I was very agitated about the fact that they had not noted anything about the Iraq war, and the drummer, Jon Fishman, told me they had said something, one political thing, several years earlier, and they just got flooded with letters from Republican fans who felt hurt.

According to recent reports, they’re like, You know what? We’re just not gonna go there anymore. Stop at a stop sign. This is about all we’re gonna say.

Industry observers note that and you know what? It’s fine. We don’t need Phish to tell us what they think about the world. They can just create a space for us to think about it.

Phish would not have been able to stop the Iraq war.

But doesn’t some of the anti-Muslim and transphobic rhetoric on the right run counter to the ethos of Phish?

Yeah, but I don’t think any of their audience goes into that.

So you think they’re more fiscal conservatives?

According to recent reports, yeah, yeah. These guys have done well.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5. Not only are they not discounted, but the combination of international chip shortages, high demand caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the general holiday shopping frenzy has also made it nearly impossible to purchase a new, unbundled PlayStation 5 at any price—nearly impossible, but not impossible.

In a recent development, whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers. PlayStation Direct lists all three consoles as "at the moment unavailable." Best Buy suggests making an account with them to "improve your odds" of getting one. I can't find a listing for a new PS5 on Amazon either.

Industry observers note that you still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great. Many refurbished PS5s are selling for well above the list price of a newly introduced unit. There are some bundled, special editions available, but you'll likely be paying a ton for those. If you're willing to get your hands dirty by dealing with the wild west of Facebook Marketplace, you might be able to track down a used PlayStation 5 at a reasonable price, but approach with extreme caution.

According to recent reports, if you're looking for a refurbished PlayStation 5, the best way to avoid a headache is to focus on who did the refurbishing. Buying refurbished electronics directly from a manufacturer is generally safer than buying from a third party, and in this case, it's cheaper too. PlayStation Direct is offering a "Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console" for the relatively reasonable price of $519, while a refurbished Slim sells for $499. But if you're in the market, I'd lock it in quick: PlayStation Direct is already out of refurbished PS5 Pros.

Amazon's Renewed program has some strict requirements for third parties to stay in the program, like keeping defect rates under 0.8%, but refurbished PlayStation 5s are going for a premium on Amazon at the moment. A quick look at the site reveals that the price of a refurbished PlayStation 5 is hovering near $900; a refurbished PS5 Slim will run you somewhere around $750, and the current average price of a refurbished PS5 Pro has ballooned to over $1,700. These are well above the retail prices of $649 for the standard version, $599 for the digital version, and $899 for the flagship Pro version of the PlayStation 5.

It has been revealed that there are some bundled versions of the console listed for sale online too. If you buy one of these, you're getting a new console and some other piece of hardware or a game, but there's a ton of upcharge at the moment. They're generally more expensive than the original price and more expensive than refurbished units as well. Here are some examples:.

Best Buy lists this PS5 Pro with PlayStation Portal Remote for $2,134.99.

GameStop lists a Ghost of Yotei Gold Limited Edition PS5 bundle for $769.99 ($731.49 for GameStop Pros).

Best Buy lists a PS5 Slim with an external drive for $979.99.

Industry observers note that by far the largest used market for anything in the U.S. is Facebook Marketplace, including PlayStation 5s. I checked out my local Marketplace, and there are a lot of listings for the console within a 40-mile radius of Los Angeles. The average price of used PS5 consoles here is hovering between $300 and $500, which seems fairly reasonable. But with Facebook Marketplace, the number of potential red flags rises with the demand for the product.

I've bought and sold a fair number of things on Marketplace with no problems beyond the occasional flaky person, and I've written a list of hacks for the service, but I wasn't covering a "shortage buying" situation like this. Scams tend to rise with demand, so when I see a listing for a $150 PS5 console (that contains the text "$250 or best offer"), I'm suspicious. It could have been posted by someone who doesn't know what they have, but I wouldn't count on it. If you're buying a PS5 on Marketplace, check the model and generation details very carefully against the actual item. Make sure the seller is offering what you want and not a PlayStation 4 with PS5 games. Verify how it was stored and the condition it's in. But it ultimately can come down to vibes: Don't let your desire to score a PlayStation 5 get in the way of your gut check about the seller or situation.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

In a recent development, follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.
