According to recent reports, the fantasy genre has become synonymous with stories that require an enormous time commitment to get through. TV indicates like Game of Thrones, Supernatural, and The Wheel of Time have made lengthy fantasy storytelling popular, but that does not mean that is all the genre has to offer. Among some of the most beloved fantasy series is a treasure trove of genre shows that only take a weekend to watch. Even with their short run times, these shows deliver an entertainment experience akin to longer series.

The best fantasy indicates are not always the longest, but those that tell their stories in a way that leaves a good impression on audiences, regardless of their length. There is always a need for a series, fantasy or not, to introduce a convincing world and characters who make its plot better instead of weighing it down. The most memorable genre shows do this, but the shorter productions do so without requiring audiences to commit to an overwhelming episode count.

Recent findings suggest that one could argue that shorter fantasy shows that can be binged in a day or two tend not to fully explore their worlds, but that is not always the case. Fantasy series with a weekend-length episode count understand their time is limited, so they don't linger on filler. All in all, it is a tricky balancing act to tell a story in a few episodes while still doing justice to what it is trying to say. Fortunately, several fantastic fantasy series have figured out just how to do this perfectly.

Recent findings suggest that dirk Gently’s Holistic Detective Agency is a Netflix show most viewers have never heard of, but it's a woefully underrated series. Best described as The Dresden Files, but with an incredible duo, the series centers around the delusionally optimistic Dirk Gently (Samuel Barnett) and his reluctant partner, Todd Brotzman (Elijah Wood), as they go about investigating supernatural crimes. Dirk Gently has everything an audience can expect from a fanatsy/sci-fi/mystery series: interesting cases, deep lore, as well as an emotional core.

However, what truly elevates the series from great to excellent is two primary protagonists, Dirk and Todd. Like any memorable TV duo, the two characters have a sort of odd-couple relationship. Where Dirk walks around like a happy puppy, Todd is sullen and doesn’t always see the bright side to everything. It is this contrast in their demeanor that makes the show so interesting and makes viewers excited about what the odd pair will do next.

Sources indicate that several people have grown up reading, watching, or listening to the stories of Cinderella, Snow White, Prince Charming, and many other fairy tale characters. With such tales being so familiar and seeing several iterations over the years, it's difficult to do something new with them that would make viewers notice, as opposed to ignoring them because they've seen the same stories time and again. The 10th Kingdom is perfect because it understood that fairy tales are interesting, but they don’t have to follow the same storytelling formula as those that have come before them.

The series centers around a young woman named Virginia (Kimberly Williams-Paisley) and her father, who are transported from modern-day Fresh York into a magical world consisting of nine fairy tale kingdoms. For a television production released in 2000, The 10th Kingdom has an impressively ambitious fantasy setting. It includes everything that audiences love about fairy tales, but also ensures it adds a bit of a modern touch.

It has been revealed that cartoons are usually frowned upon by most audiences who erroneously believe that live-action offers a better viewing experience. Cartoon Network's Over the Garden Wall disproves this theory by being a masterpiece that tells a surprisingly deep story that delves into everything from the meaning of life, and grief, to the pain of growing up. Initially, Over the Garden Wall plays out like a story about two brothers who get lost in the woods, but it is actually way more than that.

It has been revealed that the beauty of Over the Garden Wall is how audiences come away with different versions of what the meaning of the series is. Some viewers believe that the Unknown was a hallucination, while others are convinced that the series was a dream or a metaphor for death. The thing about Over the Garden Wall is that it is open to interpretation. All arguments about what the show means have some merit, which is what makes it such a joy to watch.

It has been revealed that starring David Jason and Sean Astin, The Color of Magic is a two-part British fantasy miniseries based on the first two novels in Terry Pratchett's beloved Discworld series. The story introduces viewers to Rincewind (David Jason), an exceptionally incompetent wizard who has very little magical ability and an even greater talent for getting himself into trouble. His life takes an unexpected turn when he encounters Twoflower (Sean Astin), a cheerful tourist from a distant land who has travelled to Discworld to experience its wonders.

Pratchett’s Discworld novels have one of the best fantasy settings, which ultimately means that they are not easy to bring to life. Thankfully, The Color of Magic gives it a valiant effort, resulting in a world that is so perfectly built that it is easy for non-book readers to see why the Discworld series is such a fan favorite. While The Color of Magic is an exceptional fantasy series that shines for many reasons, Rincewind makes it even better.

Recent findings suggest that most fantasy stories often revolve around powerful wizards, or individuals destined to save the world. Rincewind is practically the opposite. He is a cowardly, largely incompetent wizard whose greatest talent is running away from dangerous situations. This, of course, makes him one of the most interesting characters in fantasy TV.

It's easy to dismiss Loki as another Marvel Cinematic Universe cash grab, but the Disney+ fantasy series is much more than that. Occurring after the events of Avengers: Endgame, Loki sees the titular character stuck in the Time Variance Authority, an organization that fixes timelines, after he steals the Tesseract. The series is complex, with lots of moving parts, including the TVA and several versions of Loki. But beneath the complexity is a story about someone who has been viewed as a villain but is actually a hero.

It has been revealed that tom Hiddleston is, as one might expect, fantastic as Loki. However, he does not carry the show alone. Owen Wilson as Mobius and Sophia Di Martino as Sylvie are absolutely riveting. Loki is the perfect example of a show that proves that there is always nuance to a character. Granted, the series is a sci-fi and fantasy fan’s dream come true, but it is also an incredibly thoughtful look at a character who finally begins to understand what his purpose really is.

Released in 2024, Dead Boy Detectives is based on characters from Neil Gaiman's DC Comics universe. The eight-episode series follows two teenage ghosts, Edwin Payne (George Rexstrew) and Charles Rowland (Jayden Revri), who decide to remain on Earth after death rather than move on to the afterlife. Instead, they establish a detective agency dedicated to investigating supernatural mysteries and helping spirits resolve unfinished business.

Dead Boy Detectives doesn’t exactly tread newly introduced waters when it comes to its supernatural/mystery plot. However, it does set itself apart from others in the genre due to its two primary protagonists. Because the series centers on two teenage ghosts who have decided that death shouldn't prevent them from having careers, it is immediately entertaining.

According to recent reports, the series’ main duo give it much of its personality. Charles frequently encourages Edwin to embrace experiences beyond his investigations, while Edwin provides the intelligence and discipline necessary to solve their cases, making the duo a match made in heaven.

Recent findings suggest that arcane has been hailed as not only one of the best animated indicates of the past decade of the past decade, but also as the kind of fantasy series that other shows in the genre should aim to emulate. Premiering on Netflix in 2021, Arcane is mainly centered on the contentious relationship between two sisters: Vi (Hailee Steinfeld) and Jinx (Ella Purnell). However, as the show goes on, it becomes a story about the fight between good and evil and whether good endings can justify wrong actions.

The Netflix original series is a masterclass in world-building. Though the show only has two seasons with 18 episodes, it manages to pack so much into its limited time. The beautifully animated series is brilliant at balancing tension with the complexity of how humans relate to each other. Of course, Vi and Jinx’s relationship is at the center of it, but there are other supporting characters who are just as intriguing as the primary protagonists.

One of the most fascinating things about Arcane is that it never drops the ball. Every episode is perfect, every storyline is carefully woven, and every character gets the time they need to develop and be the kind of protagonists that audiences care about, whether they love or hate them.

Another fantasy series that demonstrates that a great duo is the heart of a memorable story, Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell centers around Mr Norrell (Eddie Marsan), a cautious, scholarly magician who believes magic should be controlled and practiced exclusively by those he considers responsible, and Jonathan Strange (Bertie Carvel), a naturally gifted young man whose extraordinary magical abilities quickly attract attention.

Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell Key Details.

Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell excellently incorporates magic into an otherwise recognizable historical setting. The series places supernatural events within an alternative version of Regency-era England. Magic is treated almost like an academic discipline, with its own history, theories, and social expectations. This, in turn, makes it a series that is already ahead of its competitors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games' UK workforce has voted firmly against unionization the week after the studio's latest game, Grand Theft Auto 6, demolished sales records.

According to recent reports, the vote was 25% in favor of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. It's a decisive result, especially considering a 93.2% turnout for the vote, with 1,544 employees from Rockstar's offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating.

The two-week ballot coincided not just with GTA 6's launch, but with an employment tribunal hearing over the firing of 31 Rockstar workers in 2025. Rockstar argued the workers had leaked tech giant secrets, while the IWGB characterized the action as union-busting. A judgment in the case is pending.

The union can continue to represent individual members, and Rockstar staff remain free to organize over pay, overtime, and other complications, but Rockstar management will not be formally required to meet or negotiate with union reps.

Rockstar Games head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement that the organization was "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.".

Sources indicate that "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

Industry observers note that in its own statement, the IWGB vowed to fight on. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union said. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One thing I think that’s really underrated about Hallmark is how the network’s projects manage to do a lot without the world’s largest budgets. (These aren't upcoming MCU movies!) Sometimes, however, a little bit of good karma wafts a production’s way just like a snowflake in the crisp winter air. This is exactly what happened on the set of Mistletoe Murders when the show found Fletcher’s Grove, the cool small town hide out Emily Lane (Sarah Drew) opens her Christmas shop in. Apparently, the show has Reacher to thank for this.

While Reacher is not known for having the insane budgets some of Amazon Prime Videos other reveals like Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power have had, the show did once create an entire facade for a small town and then left it behind after less than a month.

According to recent reports, if you’ve seen Reacher, you know the set. It’s on the Pickering Backlot in Ontario, and it was used during Season 1 to create Margrave, the fictional Georgia town that sees Jack Reacher facing the death of his brother and getting accused of murder himself. It’s a great season of TV, and it came with a pretty nice set, so nice that when Mistletoe Murders was scouting around, they thought it would be the perfect setting for Fletcher’s Grove.

Hallmark brought CinemaBlend to the set of Mistletoe Murders, where producer Michelle Melanson told me what happened, and how they fortuitously came across the former Reacher property.

It has been revealed that I believe they used it for 18 shoot days. That’s it. And then they left it. It’s on land owned by the city of Pickering, but William F. White at Sunbelt noted, ‘Well we can maybe use this, we can rent it to productions.’ So, that’s what they did, they sort of rented it to productions. And when we saw it – it’s a little small town – we were like, ‘This is Fletcher’s Grove.’.

To Amazon’s credit, there’s a little more to it than just having an excess of money to build a whole city and dump it. Season 1 of Reacher was originally expected to film in Georgia. Then, the pandemic hit and intends changed. It was easier and safer to build a little town on a spot in the middle of nowhere in Canada, and that’s exactly what the show did.

Now, it’s a bit of “backlot trivia” in Mistletoe Murders’ own story, though the Hallmark series also has its own indoor set, which helps them to control temperature while filming during hot summers. It also gives them the ability to move forward should Amazon ever want to tear down the “real” Margrave/Fletcher’s Grove.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

So that’s our little backlot trivia. We dress it up. That’s where the Mistletoe is. This year we’re excited; we have things like a Christmas market. We wanted to save ourselves because this backlot could go away at any time. They could decide they don’t want to keep it; so we built this set.

Recent findings suggest that I love it when two indicates I deeply enjoy have synergy like this. Prior to being able to visit the set of Mistletoe Murders ahead of this fall's Season 3 return on the 2026 TV schedule, I would never have known the Sarah Drew-led series would have anything in common with the Alan Ritchson series, but this is one very cool connection.

This year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is going to look a bit different. First, the threat of severe weather has prompted Macy’s to reschedule the event until Saturday, beginning at 8:30 a.m. ET. But even before the forecast turned, there was a big change: While in the past, viewers would enjoy five or so of the best performances from the current Broadway season, this year, there’s only one big Broadway number. But don’t fret, theater folk. For the milestone occasion of the parade’s 100th anniversary, the powers that be at NBC and Macy’s have put a latest spin on their tried-and-true formula, gathering the Broadway community for one supersized performance, featuring more shows and performers than ever before.

The result is an epic 10-minute medley, introduced by Julianne Hough, who will star in Damn Yankees on Broadway this spring, featuring nine beloved Broadway reveals: The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon!, and—what else?—Wicked.

Recent findings suggest that the mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous. Kitt is no stranger to writing a big production number, having cowritten the Tony Awards opening number “Bigger!,” performed by host Neil Patrick Harris with lyrics by Lin-Manuel Miranda in 2013, among other ambitious musical endeavors. Despite his previous experience, a 10-minute, nine-show medley presented a unique set of challenges the composer had yet to tackle.

A total of 133 people are performing in the medley—114 Broadway cast members, 17 dancers, a child actor, and Hough. On top of that, more than 125 other Broadway professionals—including stage managers, wardrobe supervisors, and hair and makeup teams—are on site to facilitate the production, bringing the total number of people involved to well over 250.

It has been revealed that “Most notable to me in doing something like this—to celebrate this community, this beautiful community that I’m so lucky to be a part of,” Kitt tells me. “Everyone who’s participating, you want them to feel happy and excited about what they’re doing.”.

Industry observers note that A little over a month ago, Kitt and creative producer Sarah O’Gleby got to work figuring out how to make a cohesive musical number out of nine very different indicates. He wrote the first draft of the arrangement over the course of a few days. “It was way too long,” he indicates. That might be because Kitt had to figure out how to connect these disparate shows musically while also finding room for Easter eggs for theater fans: musical nods to shows that might not otherwise be featured in the medley, including Anything Goes, The Music Man, A Chorus Line, and Kitt’s personal favorite, Into the Woods, whose music kicks things off.

“Into the Woods was one of those highlights that made me want to write for the theater,” he tells me. “The downbeat of the prologue is one of the most beautiful musical gestures; every time I hear it, I get goosebumps. So that was really special and vital for me to get to plug into, and there are so many others.”.

It has been revealed that surprisingly, it will be Kitt’s first time attending the parade in person. “The parade has meant so much to me,” he says. “I’ve watched it for years. I’ve taped it. I’m lucky enough to have shows that have been a part of it. I think that celebrating that relationship and celebrating the history of Broadway and being able to spotlight so many important shows and artists just feels very exciting and gratifying.”.

“I’m a tiny little person, but I love to do really big things,” says O’Gleby. A former performer on the West End, O’Gleby moved to the States almost two decades ago to pursue a career as a Broadway performer, dancing in revivals of Brigadoon and How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying. Now she choreographs Broadway productions like Shucked and, most recently, Pink’s widely celebrated Tony Awards opening number. Given her Broadway bona fides, she’s also intimately familiar with the magic of the parade. “I was lucky to perform on the parade as a Broadway girl and the associate choreographer and dance captain on demonstrates that I was in,” she says. “It was so wonderfully American.”.

In a recent development, the first of two rehearsals took place Friday afternoon at Pier59 Studios at Chelsea Piers. Around 4 p.m., as the sun began to set over the Hudson River, Broadway performers from different shows practiced the medley. O’Gleby, wearing silver leather pants and clutching a God mic, was charged with organizing the chaos and managing the more than 100 Broadway performers in the room. Standing offstage between a broomstick and a red Les Mis flag, I could still see traces of green makeup on the face of Wicked’s current Elphaba, Keri René Fuller. Most of the performers gathered had a show of their own to perform in just a few hours, but that didn’t stop them from giving it their all in rehearsal, onstage and off, cheering the other productions along as each got its moment in the spotlight.

According to recent reports, case in point: At the end of the rehearsal, the whole room erupted into cheers for the original cast members from Rent—including original Angel, Tony winner Wilson Jermaine Heredia, and original Joanne, Fredi Walker—who are gathering to perform “Seasons of Love” in the parade. (During the rehearsal, Aladdin’s current Genie, Sherri Shepherd, couldn’t help but mouth along to the words of the seminal song.) “It was that moment of why we’re a part of this community,” O’Gleby claims, nearly choking up. “Everyone in the room—stage managers, costume, I mean everybody in the room—the way they were applauding these original cast members and what they gave to all of us as a community, really all over the world, it was incredible.”.

At the second rehearsal, on Monday night outside on 34th Street beneath Macy’s giant turkey, the mood remained high even as the temperatures dropped. By 11 p.m., performers were bundled in winter jackets, sweatshirts, and leg warmers, with their character shoes still on. They hugged one another for warmth and jumped up and down, kicking their feet to stay loose between setups. Margaret Cho, who stars as the Narrator in The Rocky Horror Show, danced “The Time Warp” with her Chihuahua, Lucia, tucked into a pouch in her jacket, the dog’s head peeking out.

In a recent development, for O’Gleby, a smooth Monday-night rehearsal means setting each show up for success come Saturday morning and making sure all nine shows are “represented in the most powerful and clear storytelling way that we can,” she says. “This is a huge moment for these shows to sell lots of tickets so everyone gets to keep making their magic every night. And so it’s crucial to me that each team gets to communicate what they need and what they think would really make their show shine.”.

On Wednesday afternoon, Macy's announced that “after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” a disappointing piece of news for those who build their holiday around the annual event.

According to recent reports, this is only the fourth time in history that the parade hasn't been held on Thanksgiving: In 1942, 1943, and 1944 it was canceled completely as its trademark giant balloons were repurposed as part of the World War II effort. Compared to those years, a move to Saturday seems manageable, O’Gleby claims. “The weather will be what it will be, but we will delight in that and deliver the best.".

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I've seen spoilers you people wouldn't believe.
  • What's a worse fate in the world of "Blade Runner," to be human or to be a Replicant?
  • Leave it to "Blade Runner 2099" to flip yet another classic franchise staple on its head.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I've seen spoilers you people wouldn't believe. This article discusses major plot details from all eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099.".

What's a worse fate in the world of "Blade Runner," to be human or to be a Replicant? Throughout both films, organics in this post-apocalyptic setting were able to "enjoy" their time at the top of the food chain. That all changes in Prime Video's "Blade Runner 2099," the live-action story taking place after the world order has been upended and our supposed underlings have gained all the power for themselves. While Replicants were built to be "more human than human," the subtle differences between the two kinds are all but impossible to detect — on the surface, at least. But, as we know, looks can be deceiving; what's underneath is another matter entirely.

Leave it to "Blade Runner 2099" to flip yet another classic franchise staple on its head. Traditionally, the purposefully off-putting questionnaire known as the Voight-Kampff test was meant to detect whether an individual is a Replicant or not. In the sci-fi series, the rise of the Replicants and the 50 years that have passed since "Blade Runner 2049" have introduced even more changes. Enter the Index Test, an inverted form of the established quiz. But rather than differentiate between the two beings, this test is meant to detect whether the subject has developed feelings of empathy towards humans.

In Episode 5, titled "My Lord," we learn far more about this strange fresh setup than the show had previously revealed. All we ever saw was the unusually young human girl administering the test, the odd non sequiturs she posed to (supposed) Replicants like Hunter Schafer's Cora, and the results of whether they passed the baseline or not. But that, too, was only scratching the surface.

Of all the differences between humans and Replicants, empathy is the biggest of them all. "Blade Runner 2099" draws fairly stark lines in the sand between the two, with flesh-and-blood people now completely helpless before their bioengineered creations. But despite their physical advantages and killer instincts, Replicants' lack of a childhood means they're deficit in that crucial, compassionate emotion separating humans from all other living things. As we soon learn, however, Replicants can feel these strong feelings ... and actually fear it, too.

In a recent development, this is all summed up in the storyline involving Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey), the young human girl we learn has been sold off into indentured servitude and indoctrinated along with many others into administering Index Tests. Episode 5 peels back all the horrifying layers, showing us Greta's training under awfully unsettling circumstances. First, she's taken through a museum exhibit explaining the purpose and history of the Voight-Kampff test, used by human Blade Runners to hunt Replicants. Now, the new status quo means Replicants use this new Index Test to police their own kind — and, as one instructor explains, prevent any "emotional contagion" crossing over from humans to their Replicant overlords.

Sources indicate that it's a fascinating idea with some pretty serious implications for our two main characters. Michelle Yeoh's Olwen is currently undergoing some serious emotional turmoil herself, as her search for the missing Replicant and her secret lover Marek (Johnny Harris) ends in his tragic death. Meanwhile, Cora's own emotional attachments makes it only a matter of time before her human identity is made known. As a result, every time they sit down for the Index Test makes for must-watch TV.

All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are streaming on Prime Video.

‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the middle of “All of a Sudden,” Mari (Tao Okamoto) pulls out a whiteboard and markers to diagram the principles of nature vs.
  • While a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients.
  • And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is an unorthodox sequence. In the middle of “All of a Sudden,” Mari (Tao Okamoto) pulls out a whiteboard and markers to diagram the principles of nature vs. capitalism for her fresh friend Marie-Lou (Virginie Efira). The scene lasts 11 minutes and digs into material you would expect in a university seminar, not the latest cinematic achievement from the Oscar-winning director of “Drive My Car,” Ryūsuke Hamaguchi.

While a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients. Related Stories How Much of Quentin Tarantino’s Scrapped Film ‘The Movie Critic’ Made It Into ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? Robert Aramayo’s Star-Making Turn in ‘I Swear’ Is Already Award-Winning, Now He Just Wants People to See It.

And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes. Now, its distributor, Neon, heads into this weekend’s holiday theatrical release believing it has a legit shot at winning over the more commercially oriented Oscar voters — and becoming one of the (increasingly common) foreign-language Best Picture nominations. Neon similarly released “Sentimental Value” and “The Secret Agent” to Best Picture nominations the year before.

According to recent reports, the whiteboard scene is not an extraneous aside, but a critical turning point in the women’s relationship. We asked the film’s writer/director why it not only works, but was deemed vital to the film.

“In trying to answer why this somehow works, I think there’s a few layers to it,” stated Hamaguchi while on IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “And one maybe is because it really is something that is far removed from what is generally considered as cinematic. Perhaps because of that, it brings about a certain suspense, where you wonder, ‘OK, what is this for? What is this actually going to do?’ And there’s a certain sense of wondering that happens.”.

The scene comes a little over an hour into the film. Neither woman wants their magical evening to end. Mari follows Marie-Lou to her job as director of a nursing home, where she struggles to implement her passion project, “Huminitude,” a patient-centered care method based on touch and eye contact, which Mari sees in action. What prompts Mari’s whiteboard seminar is an attempt to help her fresh companion put into perspective the resistance she faces in implementing Huminitude and open the door to problem-solving.

“I think the second part [of why the scene works] really comes down to the efforts of the actors that are performing this scene,” said Hamaguchi of Okamoto and Efira, who shared the Best Actress Prize at Cannes. “For Tao, I think it was an incredibly difficult scene to perform because first of all she really needed to understand all of the concepts that she was describing here and to really understand everything intellectually. And so in her preparation she did read a lot of the relevant books to really understand what she is talking about.”.

Hamaguchi believes the key to his dialogue-driven film is not necessarily how the words are spoken, but the performance of the listening and how the words are received. In Efira’s whiteboard scene, we see a shift from determined frustration to open enthusiasm that changes the direction of the film itself.

“The attitude of listening that Virginie portrays in this moment, I think, is very important and really supports this scene,” mentioned Hamaguchi. “She’s not uninterested in what is going on, but in fact she feels that this is something that she should really be exploring together and she’s there and very much present. And I think this attitude of interest and curiosity really starts to work on the audience as well. And so in that sense I think ultimately this scene really works because of the actors’ performances.”.

One topic that comes up in most post-screening Q&As is that both actresses were not working in the native language. Hamaguchi himself had to work with an interpreter to direct his leads. This is not the first time Hamaguchi has worked this way. On the podcast, he stated that, in his experience directing the play inside “Drive My Car,” the language barrier was less of a hindrance and could even aid actors in listening to one another, as shown in the whiteboard scene.

“I felt that, in fact, this kind of difficulty that exists can in fact provide an environment for even more heightened concentration than you might have if you were speaking the same language,” remarked Hamaguchi. “ I think that actually when you can actually hear a lot and get a lot of information from somebody’s voice, you can, in fact, precisely feel just how concentrated the person is when they’re saying something by listening to their voice.”.

Asked if any of his collaborators or producers ever questioned the whiteboard scene after reading the script, Hamaguchi remarked no, and speculated why: “Because it’s so unusual, I think people understood that this is something that I really wanted to do.”.

According to recent reports, “There were some questions around, ‘This section feels a little long. Is there anything we can do about that?’” recalled Hamaguchi, adding that he made a concerted effort to cut his four-hour script to a three-hour, 16-minute running time.

It has been revealed that “For me, I was ultimately trying to bring in the shortest version that I felt was accurate for this moment. But ultimately, there is this understanding that this moment is a very notable turning point within the film, and so I believe that the producers also understood this.”.

“All of a Sudden” is now playing in select theaters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

DC reveals the identity of the Batman villain who will act as the Dark Knight's main antagonist in an upcoming crossover story. Despite the huge size of Batman's rogues' gallery, a select group of Gotham criminals are recurring main villains across all media. The Joker is ubiquitous, with primary antagonistic appearances in virtually every DC continuity. Other foes like Two-Face, the Riddler, the Penguin, and Bane pop up in dozens of DC comics, movies, and series, followed closely by Scarecrow, Ra’s al Ghul, Mr. Freeze, and mob kingpins Carmine Falcone and Sal Maroni.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, dozens of memorable Gotham villains almost always get relegated to brief cold-open beatdowns or henchman muscle. Physical powerhouses like Clayface, Killer Croc, Solomon Grundy, and Man-Bat have never fought Batman in a theatrical movie, and they usually act as mid-level boss fights or hired muscle in other media. Likewise, psychological and gimmick rogues like the Mad Hatter, Ventriloquist and Scarface, Professor Pyg, Hugo Strange, Firefly, Calendar Man, and Hush rarely get the chance to headline a major mainstream adaptation on their own.

Other Batman enemies are even less lucky, with zero main antagonist appearances to their name. Fortunately, DC is finally placing one of those Gotham criminals in the spotlight with a major twist that makes them a threat not only to Batman, but also to Superman, Wonder Woman, Supergirl, and many other heroes.

Industry observers note that dark Knights of Steel II #5 reveals a shocking new villain when Prince Victor Falcone, the unstable son of Blüdhaven’s honorable ruler King Carmine Falcone, reveals himself to be Victor Zsasz and kills his father to claim the throne. Zsasz had already shown his sadistic nature in issue #1, when he slaughtered young Bruce Wayne’s hound Ace. Now, Victor makes his move while the House of El mourns Queen Lara and Amanda Waller sits imprisoned. In a ruthless coup straight out of Game of Thrones, Victor murders his own father, carves a fresh tally scar directly into his own flesh to commemorate the kill, and seizes the Blüdhaven crown as "the Mad King Zsasz.".

Dark Knights of Steel II's change to Zsasz' lineage isn't the first modification of this kind, as this universe's Alfred never really existed.

With King Jor-El and Queen Lara gone, Blüdhaven’s throne immediately makes Zsasz a geopolitical nightmare for Bruce Wayne, Kal-El, Zala-El, and every realm. King Victor Zsasz now has access to an entire kingdom’s armies and resources, while the House of El is weakened and divided. Zsasz’s signature self-scarring obsession is a terrifying match to his newfound sovereign royal power and his personal malice toward Bruce Wayne in this timeline.

Victor Zsasz has a brief Arkham inmate cameo in Batman Begins, a secondary antagonist role in the DCEU's Birds of Prey, appears as a recurring mob enforcer in Gotham, and has minor side-missions in the Arkham video games. He has always possessed the psychological ingredients of a standout thriller villain, including his nihilistic worldview, his eerie intelligence hidden behind quiet patience, and a chilling ritual of carving tally marks into his own skin that makes his run-ins with Batman intensely personal and unsettling. However, Zsasz has never been trusted to carry a major storyline on his own.

Recent findings suggest that tom Taylor and Otto Schmidt’s bold decision to turn Victor Zsasz into a kingdom-threatening tyrant in Dark Knights of Steel II #5 serves as a subtle reminder of how many other overlooked Batman rogues could thrive if given a similar main-villain spotlight in future Elseworlds or mainline sagas. Villains like Calendar Man, Professor Pyg, Firefly, and Deacon Blackfire all have their own psychological hooks and theatrical menace that usually get sidelined in favor of another Joker or Riddler scheme. At least in alternative timelines, these underused antagonists can make Batman’s rogues' gallery feel truly varied.

Sorry Jason And Lucia, These 5 GTA 6 Side Characters Steal Every Scene They're In

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that although Jason and Lucia are the stars of Grand Theft Auto 6 and amazing characters in their own right, there are lots of side characters who steal the show whenever they show up.
  • These side characters make the world of GTA 6 feel more fleshed out, lived in, and representative of all different kinds of kooky folk.
  • It has been revealed that brian is the single biggest scene-stealer in GTA 6 for one reason: Stephen freakin’ Root!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that although Jason and Lucia are the stars of Grand Theft Auto 6 and amazing characters in their own right, there are lots of side characters who steal the show whenever they show up. From folks critical to the main story path to weirdos you meet if you take the time to stop and chat with someone on the side of the road, GTA 6 constantly introduces wild, memorable characters almost every hour.

These side characters make the world of GTA 6 feel more fleshed out, lived in, and representative of all different kinds of kooky folk. They’re a major part of what makes the game special, and we’re thankful that Rockstar Games took the time to make us care about people other than Jason and Lucia. In particular, these five characters emerged as some of the Polygon staff’s favorites.

It has been revealed that brian is the single biggest scene-stealer in GTA 6 for one reason: Stephen freakin’ Root! For years, Root has been one of Hollywood’s ultimate “Hey, it's that guy” character actors. Now, fresh off an extremely well-deserved Emmy win for his role in Widow’s Bay, he brings the same kinetic, frenetic energy to Brian in GTA 6.

The eternal brilliance of Root’s acting comes from the humanity he injects into every character — often people who would be impossible to believe in lesser hands. Like many of Root’s best roles, Brian is a little too wacky for the real world, but there is a clear and nuanced sense of humanity underneath all of that eccentricity. That ethos is reflected throughout the entirety of Grand Theft Auto, and Brian is the key to selling it from the start. —Ari Notis.

Recent findings suggest that of all the side characters Rockstar has introduced in GTA 6, Raul Bautista (voiced by Manny Pérez) is my personal favorite. He commands attention — not through loud bravado, but through quiet, seasoned authority. Raul carries himself around with a sun-bleached cool reminiscent of Don Johnson’s Sonny Crockett mixed with the criminal smarts of Robert De Niro’s Nick Wells from The Score. Raul isn’t the sort of guy who needs to announce himself or make a show of what he can do. As a seasoned bank heister who knows Vice City like the back of his hand, Raul operates with understated confidence and stays deliberately out of the spotlight, treating high-stakes scores like a craft rather than a spectacle.

According to recent reports, living on a boat also shows he’s calculated down to his quarters and can pull anchor and disappear on a dime whenever the heat closes in. What makes him especially intriguing is how little we know about his past. Who knows? He could’ve easily crossed paths with Michael Townley and Trevor Philips during their early heisting days — and maybe even learned a thing or two from them. — Ryan Epps.

Midway through GTA 6, just as the heists are heating up, Jason becomes an accidental hip-hop mogul. In a series of missions, Jason is called upon to help promote Real Dimez, an up-and-coming rap duo managed by Only Raw Records. The group immediately steals the show the moment they first appear on screen. Played by real Miami rappers Hood Brat and Krissy Celess, Bae-Luxe and Roxy add some welcome levity to the story as they try to get their big break with a ridiculous single about “booty holes.”.

Their missions have Jason doing promo photo shoots, breaking into house parties, and shooting music videos as Real Dimez rise to stardom. In a game that’s almost entirely about complex criminal enterprises, it’s a reprieve to get a side-tale about two musical misfits looking for their moment the old-fashioned way. — Giovanni Colantonio.

Jason’s Key Lento neighbor Shirley is a good, kind soul, if a slightly eccentric one. She has her own way of viewing the world, and while it’s certainly centered around a brand of logic unique to Shirley, it’s not a bad thing. She cares about people as much as she cares about her obnoxiously yappy little dog Arugula, and she’s genuinely hurt by the unnecessarily rude comments from Peggy (of “steal her scooter” fame).

Sources indicate that shirley is basically your odd-but-sweet neighbor who you might dread catching the attention of on your way home, but would never dream of showing that dread or turning down a chance to talk to, if only briefly. Hurting her feelings? Inconceivable. And it’s to GTA 6's credit that it encourages you to meet Shirley halfway and be kind to her without judging her oddities. — Josh Broadwell.

In a recent development, when I pulled up to my first street race in Vice City, I was not expecting to kick off a whole Fast & Furious-like sidequest in the game. Early on, you meet Yago, a talkative and ambitious racer who just has one problem: he can’t drive very well. Yago takes an instant liking to Jason, who guides him through being a better street racer and drug dealer. What ensues is one of the best male friendships in the game — and one that you can entirely miss.

Industry observers note that yago and Jason’s dynamic is equal parts hilarious and endearing, as Yago constantly teeters on annoying but is so gung-ho and into Jason that you can’t help but love him. He also exposes a softer side of Jason that you otherwise only see through his interactions with Lucia. I won’t spoil how Yago’s sidequests ultimately play out, but that event ultimately recontextualizes his entire relationship with Jason and ends up making him one of the game’s more nuanced characters. — Tomas Franzese.

Breaking: Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a big enough challenge.
  • It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget.
  • It has been revealed that as such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in new directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a big enough challenge. Doing so on the small screen adds an extra element of difficulty. Incredibly, "Blade Runner 2099" has overcome the odds to deliver yet another intoxicating excursion into the techno-industrial urban decay-scape so magically realized back in 1982's "Blade Runner" and so faithfully recreated in 2017's "Blade Runner 2049." As such, the Blade Runner franchise is now surely the most consistent on-screen sci-fi saga ever made. (Setting aside sci-fi sagas that are directed by the same person the whole time, like James Cameron's "Avatar.").

It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget. Yet director Ridley Scott and his production team managed to create one of the most believable and immersive worlds in cinema history. The famous "Hades" opening shot immediately plunges you into a future post-ecological collapse, in which technology seems to have almost grown on the wreckage of a fallen world like moss on fallen trees. The debris of society is adorned with neon and machinery, creating an environment in which past and future collide. "Blade Runner" might have been buried at the box office by "E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial," but it was an absolutely enthralling sci-fi adventure that came to define the genre.

It has been revealed that as such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in new directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle. The "Dune" director's take on the world first introduced to audiences in 1982 was immediately familiar as the same one in which Harrison Ford's Rick Deckard did battle with Rutger Hauer's Roy Batty and his band of rogue Replicants. Yet it also felt appropriately evolved for the three-decade time jump. Surely "Blade Runner 2099" couldn't pull off the same trick — especially across eight episodes? Well, it has.

Recent findings suggest that /Film's Bill Bria has hailed "Blade Runner 2099" as the best sci-fi show in years, and it's hard to disagree based solely on the production design. From the moment the show begins, we're immersed in the same world to which Ridley Scott introduced us back in 1982. In fact, "2099" recreates the "Hades" sequence so faithfully you'd think you were watching the original. It's a clever move, too. As the camera slow-zooms on the Tyrell Corporation building and evokes the tone and feel of Scott's film, it establishes "2099" as very much belonging to the "Blade Runner" legacy. But we soon discover that this is not Rick Deckard's future.

Recent findings suggest that 80 years after Harrison Ford's Blade Runner absconded with Rachael (Sean Young), Replicants have now overthrown their human masters to become the dominant race. It's a major change that refreshes the franchise and helps make it more relevant than it's ever been at a time when the looming AI garbage future has prompted widespread talk of machines taking our jobs.

As such, it's more important than ever to maintain a tone and design language that's consistent with what came before, so as to reassure fans of the saga that this isn't some sort of wholesale reinvention of the franchise they love, but an evolution that plays out in the same world. "Blade Runner 2099" impressively pulls that off with its opening scene, and it only gets better from there.

Industry observers note that when it comes to the world of "Blade Runner," fans know the deal: Retro futurism and cyberpunk aesthetics meet noirish expressionism in a technological nightmare future. Many franchises have tried to emulate the aesthetic to varying degrees of success, but there is only one "Blade Runner." As Christopher Nolan once told the Directors Guild of America while discussing Ridley Scott's film, it conjures "that feeling that there was this whole world outside the frame of the scene. You really felt there were things going on outside of those rooms where you've seen the film take place.".

In a recent development, "Blade Runner 2099" has somehow managed to make every one of its scenes feel like they belong in that same world. With that in mind, it's truly remarkable how consistent the Blade Runner universe has remained across almost a half-century's worth of projects, each of which has been separated by many years. Even the best sci-fi franchises struggle to pull off what is, admittedly, an almost impossible trick.

It has been revealed that the "Terminator" movies have never been able to recapture the intoxicating, doom-laden sci-fi slasher tone that made the first two films so memorable. The "Alien" franchise, meanwhile, has made a point of switching up its style and tone with each successive film — though more recent projects have tried to evoke the feeling of the 1979 original. "Blade Runner" films, however, all feel part of a cohesive whole that gives the entire saga this uncanny sense of existing in a real alternate timeline somewhere — as if we're witnessing an epic, decades-spanning dream play out in the mind of a dying Replicant. Regardless of how you feel about "2099" as a whole, its visual and tonal achievements simply can't be denied.

"Blade Runner 2099" Season 1 is now streaming on Prime Video.

Kerry Kennedy is not in Milan on political business, but it’s hard to rein in the enthusiasm of some Americans following the 2026 midterm elections. Democrats won decisive majorities in both the House and Senate, along with 24 of the 36 governors elections held this month. It was a blue tsunami. Kennedy—a lawyer and human rights activist born in 1959 to dynasty Democrats Robert and Ethel Kennedy—is in a celebratory mood.

She’s in town for one night only to attend a charity dinner in support of her foundation, the Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center. But first she sits down with Vanity Fair Italia, and over the course of our chat, she takes her beloved poodle, Scamper, for a short walk; sips two cappuccinos (strictly decaf), one of them iced (she apologizes to the Italians present); eats some gianduiotti chocolates; gestures animatedly; and smooths her very blonde hair.

But above all, she never stops smiling: “In America you can only go so far in the attempt to avoid the rule of law and erode democracy,” she states, making clear that her political statements are delivered in her personal capacity, “because at a certain point, even if you’re the most powerful and the richest man there, democracy will bring you down. [The president] made a mess all over the world, but in the end, in America, democracy was stronger.”.

From left: Robert Kennedy Jr., Joseph P Kennedy Jr., Tory Kennedy, and Kerry Kennedy on January 1, 1994.

Congress has the power of the purse, and now it’s going to exercise that power. But….

Ethel Kennedy and daughter Kerry Kennedy circa 1979.

A few days later, my mother got an anonymous letter saying, “Your children will be next.” She took her three oldest kids, put them in the back of her car, drove them to the Capitol, walked into the hearing room, and sat in the front row while daddy was interrogating Jimmy Hoffa, the head of the Teamsters.

According to recent reports, she was saying, “You’re not going to get to me through my children, and you’re not going to get to my husband through me. We are a fortress and we’re coming after you.” I don’t know how she grappled with the trauma.

Should you buy the Amazon Kids Kindle or a standard Paperwhite for your child? Here’s what’s different

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There comes a point when your child is old enough to potentially get their own Kindle, mostly so they stop stealing yours and filling up your library with Significant Nate collections.
  • Now is the perfect time to find the right Kindle for your child, as Amazon typically puts many of its Kindles on sale for Black Friday.
  • Unfortunately, none of them are on sale, and in general they're more expensive than their "adult" counterparts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There comes a point when your child is old enough to potentially get their own Kindle, mostly so they stop stealing yours and filling up your library with Significant Nate collections.

Now is the perfect time to find the right Kindle for your child, as Amazon typically puts many of its Kindles on sale for Black Friday. You may not have known that Amazon has kid versions of the Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft.

Unfortunately, none of them are on sale, and in general they're more expensive than their "adult" counterparts. But Amazon also offers a bit more out of the box with the kid versions.

Let's break down what you get with the Kid Kindle and why the higher price may be worth it.

To be up front, as far as we can tell, the different Kindle Kids eReaders are the same hardware that you get with the standard Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft.

The difference is that the Kid version comes with a case included. Right now, the Paperwhite Kids can be purchased with the Pirate theme, "Bookman," or Lakeside Retreat.

Industry observers note that additionally, the Kid Kindles come with a 1-year Kids+ subscription included. Basically, this is a more curated version of Kindle Plus (the rebranded of Kindle Unlimited) for children. It includes thousands of books for kids ages 6 through 12, like the Percy Jackson series or Diary of a Wimpy Kid. Also, the Kid version does not come with ads or distractions.

The Kid Kindles also have parent controls that can be accessed through the Parent Dashboard mobile app which can be used to suggest books or set screen limits.

According to recent reports, amazon updated most of its Kindle lineup earlier this year, but the 2024 version of the Kindle Paperwhite Kids is still available and the only Kids eReader on sale at $149. This version comes with 16GB of storage, a case, 6 months of Amazon Kids+, and a waterproof design.

By comparison, the adult Kindles do not come with a case, only three months of Kindle+ (which adds a cost), and you have to choose ad-supported or without lockscreen ads (again more expensive).

Sources indicate that there are content controls and parent controls on normal Kindles, but in my experience, it's more finicky and usually requires a separate account if you truly want to lock things down. Quite annoying when you're sharing with your child and your wife is filling the library with romantasy novels. Not yet, buddy, not yet.

Both the kids and adult versions can be used to access library books through the Libby app, literally the best thing about Kindles compared to most other eReaders.

According to recent reports, here's the significant difference: price. Let's use the Kindle Paperwhite as our example.

Recent findings suggest that the Ad-free, 3-month Kindle+, Paperwhite costs $219 when its not on sale. The ad-supported version costs $199. The newly introduced Kids Kindle Paperwhite costs $229.

Recent findings suggest that for a less expensive option, the cheapest standard Kindle is $149, while the Kids version costs $179. The case adds up the Kids version, but if you want a case for the adult version, the cheapest one I saw on Amazon tacks on $21 to the price.

If money isn't as big of a concern, the Kids Kindle Colorsoft is $299 but is great for kids who starting to read comic books or if you want the option for color stories. The base adult Colorsoft starts at $289 but there is a bundle with a case for $301, which is on sale.

According to recent reports, amazon refreshed the Kids Kindle this year with a thinner and lighter version. It features a 6-inch glare-free display, a themed case, and 1-year of Kids+ subscription. The Kids Kindle has up to 6 weeks of battery life and you can listen to audio books using Bluetooth headphones. Parents can control settings with the Parent dashboard.

The big difference is that I rarely see the Kid versions go on sale while the standard Kindles get discounted throughout the year typically around Black Friday, the upcoming Spring sale and the big Prime Day summer sale.

In a recent development, also, the subscription. You get three months of Kindle+ which normally costs $11.99 per month (or $143.88) for a year. The Kid Kindle comes with 12 months of Kids+, which normally costs $7.99 a month for Prime Members or $8.99 if you don't have an account.

Additionally, if you have other Amazon devices like the Amazon Kids Echo or an Amazon Kids tablet, your Kids+ subscription is accessible across each device with a child profile.

The upfront costs of the Kid Kindle is higher in general, but over the first year, if you keep the subscription, you're paying on par with the adult Kindle and getting more control and curation.

As we noted above, you don't have to get the newest model and Amazon has done a decent job of supporting much older Kindles.

In this case, don't let the sticker shock get to you and consider the Kindle Kid, Kindle Paperwhite Kid, or Kindle Colorsoft Kid for your child.

Breaking: The Cliff Booth Movie Brings Back Two Key Characters From Once Upon A Time In Hollywood

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".
  • "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher.
  • Part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher. But still, you had to wonder if any other familiar faces would pop up in this new mis-adventure.

Part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history. Thanks to the actions of Cliff, actress Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie) is not murdered by the Manson family. How does the entertainment world and Los Angeles change by 1977, when "Cliff Booth" takes place, because of that ripple effect? Tarantino wrote the script for "Cliff Booth," and if any filmmaker is equipped to dig into the nitty-gritty of such a change in Hollywood history, down to the most obscure B-pictures and forgotten TV, it's him.

Recent findings suggest that now, the major supporting cast of "Cliff Booth" is totally different. Cliff's best friend, actor Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) — for whom Cliff worked as a stunt double and driver back in 1969 — does not appear due to DiCaprio declining a cameo appearance. The movie mentions a few times that Rick moved to Australia and is at the moment starring in a popular TV show there, "Dingo Dan." Tarantino has also devised some stories about what happened to Rick after that fateful August 9, 1969 night.

But a few of the fictionalized Hollywood characters return for brief cameos: Margot Robbie as Sharon Tate, Timothy Olyphant as actor James Stacy, and even Nicholas Hammond as TV director Sam Wanamaker (in a smaller role).

One of the Quentin Tarantino Easter eggs in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is a commercial for Red Apple Cigarettes, a fictional brand that appears in other Tarantino movies. The actress in the commercial is Sharon Tate, with Cliff smiling at her and likely recalling how he saved her life. "Once Upon A Time In Hollywood" cast Sharon Tate in an angelic light, down to giving her the happy ending that reality didn't. But revisiting her in greater depth, like what became of her marriage to Roman Polanski or how her acting career played out, would risk adding a dash of salt to that sweet ending.

Industry observers note that the alternate history of Sharon Tate in "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" earned obvious comparisons to Tarantino's "Inglourious Basterds," which also starred Brad Pitt (as Lieutenant Aldo Raine, leader of the Nazi-killing Basterds). In that movie, Adolf Hitler (Martin Wutke) dies at the hands of Jewish soldiers instead of by suicide. That leads into Timothy Olyphant's "Cliff Booth" cameo, which feels self-recursively inspired by "Basterds.".

In a recent development, "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" mixes real Hollywood history with pastiche. Much of the first half sees Dalton filming a guest spot on a TV Western, "Lancer," which was a real show back in the late '60s. Olyphant appears as the real-life star of "Lancer," James Stacy, and the episode is directed by Nicholas Hammond's Sam Wanamaker, the real director of the "Lancer" pilot episode. "Cliff Booth" gives us another glimpse of Stacy and Wanamaker working in this alternate timeline's television industry.

Since 1969, Cliff Booth has become a fixer: someone who (violently) solves problems for Hollywood fixtures wrapped up with criminals. Fictional TV star Charlie Winters (Scott Caan) becomes one of his clients. The movie includes a newsreel style montage, narrated by Quentin Tarantino himself, recounting Winters' rise to TV stardom.

Sources indicate that one of Winters' highlights is "Enemy Territory," about a U.S. pilot trapped behind enemy lines in Europe during World War 2. The narrator describes the show as "'The Fugitive' with Nazis, but 'The Fugitive' with Nazis is a fun idea." (I'd watch it!) We see Winters shooting a scene where his character threatens a Gestapo officer into helping him rescue a captured American general. The officer is played by none other than Timothy-Olyphant-as-James-Stacy, doing a broad German accent with a high pitch reminiscent of Christoph Waltz's Colonel Hans Landa from "Inglourious Basterds.".

Sam Wanamaker is directing the scene. Stacy's performance is being criticized as "a smidge cavalier" — so Winters puts a live round in the prop gun with which his character is threatening the Gestapo officer. Stacy, sure enough, begins acting like a man whose life is being balanced on the edge of a trigger.

Casting Olyphant as James Stacy was a nod to how his real most famous roles are on Western TV indicates — namely, Sheriff Seth Bullock in HBO's "Deadwood" and Deputy U.S. Marshal Raylan Givens in the Kentucky-set neo-Western "Justified." But Olyphant has got range beyond playing cowboys, and his comic energy in his "Cliff Booth" cameo is just more evidence of that.

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is playing in theaters, with a Netflix release date of December 23, 2026.

In a recent development, starring Ed Weeks as Charles and Allegra Edwards as Liz, Eternally Yours took an unconventional approach to a family-centered sitcom. For tonight, however, CBS' Thursday night is going to be missing all of its usual sitcom action, including Eternally Yours.

Recent findings suggest that after seven straight weeks of Eternally Yours on Thursday nights at 8:30 p.m. ET, the newly introduced comedy is taking its first break of the fall. The consistency over the past two months, as well as the pairing with Georgie & Mandy's First Marriage, undoubtedly helped Eternally Yours carve out a niche in primetime despite replacing Ghosts. That noted, CBS pulling Eternally Yours from primetime this week isn't a sign that the show is running out of steam.

Many network TV shows skip new episodes during the week of Thanksgiving, and Eternally Yours isn't the only CBS show that's not airing a fresh installment tonight. Georgie & Mandy and Cupertino are entirely off this week, and Elsbeth will air a rerun. The network's entire Thursday night lineup will be missing new episodes. Instead, CBS will broadcast The JLo Show, a concert special showcasing Jennifer Lopez, from 8 p.m. to 10 .m. ET.

Fortunately, Eternally Yours isn't taking a long time off. The next upcoming episode will air on Thursday, December 3 in the usual 8:30 p.m. ET time slot on CBS. Called "Guess Who's Coven to Dinner," the episode will feature more of the family than usual. Charles and Liz likely won't be too thrilled, but it should make for some solid comedy before the end of the fall season. CBS' logline reveals:.

When Max’s parents arrive for a surprise visit, it leads to the discovery of a surprising and uncomfortable connection with one of the coven members. Meanwhile, now that his human wife, Phyllis, has been brought into the circle of trust, Jesse worries she’ll want to become a vampire too.

Recent findings suggest that in a fun twist, another sitcom star will return to the network as a guest star in the eighth episode of season 1. As another treat, "Guess Who's Coven to Dinner" won't be the final episode of the fall.

The fall finale will air the next week, on December 10, and CBS has already confirmed when Eternally Yours will be back in 2027. For now, fans can just look forward to what the newly introduced episode brings after the comedy's Thanksgiving break.

Latest Update: The 14 Best Star Wars Games of All Time, Ranked

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982.
  • Play it on: PlayStation 4, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.
  • It has been revealed that people like Star Wars for different reasons, from the hero’s journey, to the beautiful planet environments and the thrilling space battles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium, encompassing everything from role-playing games and first-person shooters to arcade racers and XCOM clones (the latter of two seeing well-regard releases just this year). No matter the year or the hardware, some of the best Star Wars games are worth revisiting. Here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time, ranked.

Play it on: PlayStation 4, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

It has been revealed that people like Star Wars for different reasons, from the hero’s journey, to the beautiful planet environments and the thrilling space battles. A lot of the best Star Wars games tend to narrow their scope rather than focusing on everything at once, and Squadrons definitely prioritized at shootouts in the vast reaches of space. It dropped players in cockpits that might have featured in the original movies and let players feel like they were in the middle of an operation… especially when they had a VR headset equipped. The online component was initially another compelling reason to play, but activity levels have dropped off in the years since launch. Still, it has a lot to offer if you don’t mind a more solitary experience.

Play it on: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

Recent findings suggest that respawn Entertainment has had multiple chances to do Star Wars justice, starting with this first entry in the Star Wars Jedi series. It introduces Cal Kestis, a hero living through the dark period following Revenge of the Sith. Not everyone loves the Jedi, even at the best of times. They feel a bit like the galaxy’s superheroes, and yet there’s no denying the thrill of a good lightsaber duel. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order focuses on that aspect in particular, and lets players explore interesting environments other games only allow them to glimpse from afar. It’s pretty and fun, despite performance issues at launch and some tedious backtracking.

Play it on: PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X.

If you’re going to build a strategy game to entertain audiences in a post-XCOM world, you can do a lot worse for inspiration. Star Wars Zero Company took some winning elements from that venerated franchise and transported them to a galaxy far, far away. The result is one of the greatest Star Wars games ever created, featuring compelling turn-based combat and a generally satisfying plot centered in the Clone Wars era. Some players felt the exploration segments between battles introduced unwelcome filler. And the battles themselves sometimes were a little too easy to maintain tension. But such faults, as well as technical complications at launch that included camera issues and performance drops, were minor blemishes on an otherwise standout experience that leaves us hoping for a similarly spectacular sequel.

Play it on: PlayStation 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox.

Following closely after Star Wars: Starfighter, which released one year prior, Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter added Force abilities that proved devastating in space battles. The arsenal of weapons expanded, plus a full split-screen cooperative campaign added a latest dimension to the experience. Critics at the time weren’t impressed by how much of the experience felt like the previous game, though, and the disjointed storyline couldn’t match what came before it. Even so, it served as a worthy follow-up and was better than its predecessor in some key ways. Jedi Starfighter is easy to play on a PlayStation 4, as well, despite the date of its original release.

When word first arrived that BioWare was working on another Star Wars RPG set in the Old Republic, visions of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic danced in our heads. However, we eventually learned that Star Wars: The Old Republic would actually take the form of an MMORPG, which dulled some of that early enthusiasm. Fortunately, the game turned out much better than it easily might have, even if it did sometimes feel like World of Warcraft in disguise and initially lacked a meaningful endgame. When early subscription numbers faltered, Electronic Arts explored a free-to-play model, allowing it to build the following it needed to justify continued development. Since then, the game has seen additional content drops, even after Disney’s acquisition of Lucasfilm. If you are so inclined, you can experience much of that content for free, thanks to the ongoing stewardship of Broadsword Online Games.

Play it on: Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

Lego Star Wars was a surprise hit when it arrived for PlayStation 2. A variety of sequels since then have also proven to be great fun. The Skywalker Saga is the biggest release of the lot, presenting a fresh take on the stories in all nine movies about the Skywalker family and their friends. Rather than compiling and touching up everything that came before (which is partly contained in Lego Star Wars: The Complete Saga), it presents the classic stories with a thoroughly modern touch. Some of the older elements, like a fixed camera and confusing level progression, have been cleaned up for the 2022 release. The much larger and more complex level hubs are also a satisfying development. Such improvements make The Skywalker Saga the definitive way to see your favorite Star Wars heroes doing heroic things in plastic brick form. The game is also a terrific option if you’re looking for something you can play with your less experienced friends or even small children, as one might expect from the Lego games, though the second player sometimes must take a back seat while the main hero does the tricky stuff.

A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Play it on: Nintendo 64, Windows PC.

When Star Wars: Rogue Squadron released on the Nintendo 64, you had to buy the hardware’s mostly optional “expansion pak” to play it as the development team at Factor 5 intended. That’s how you knew you were getting something good. The added RAM brought various locations from around the Star Wars universe to life, filling them with enemy turrets and walkers that were prime targets for your lasers and rockets. The addictive gameplay loop kept college guys like me playing well into the early morning hours… and I certainly wasn’t alone. Today, the visuals are dated, but the stages still bring those memories roaring back. It’s enough to make a person want to download the Steam version and play it all over again.

Play it on: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

The second Star Wars Jedi game from Respawn Entertainment offered more of what we loved about the first one: numerous approaches to lightsaber combat, more open and expansive maps, and a welcome fast-travel mechanic. The story lingered near the starting line a bit longer than it should have, and some of the bosses ratcheted up the difficulty a bit unevenly. Technical issues held the experience back near launch, as well. But patches have smoothed away most of the rough edges, allowing Star Wars Jedi: Survivor to become the first-rate adventure it always deserved to be.

Play it on: PlayStation 2, PSP, Windows PC, Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that star Wars: Battlefront 2 and its predecessor are sufficiently beloved that years later, a separate developer brought them back for another go around. The original 2005 release is the one we remember most fondly, however. It let players loose on massive maps, where they could roam on foot or commandeer powerful vehicles with their friends and wreak havoc on their enemies. Although there wasn’t a lot of the depth and customization we expect from more modern shooters, the barely controlled mayhem made up for it, turning players into the architects of numerous memorable moments in one battle after another. It was arcade fun at its best, an experience the 2017 edition couldn’t quite replicate, whatever its strengths.

Play it on: PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X.

Recent findings suggest that in classic games like Burnout and F-Zero X, players became involved in spectacular crashes, amidst high-speed races through simple but spectacular terrain. One might say the same thing of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, our pick for the best arcade racing game in a generation. It brings a similar philosophy to the classics that came before it but applies it to landspeeders, pod racers, and speeder bikes. The game’s biggest innovation might be the lack of restarts mid-race, which raises the stakes as you careen around every sharp corner and fight for every burst of speed along the straightaways. Each latest vehicle you master requires different skills and comes with its own quirks, which adds variety to the experience. Venues come from a limited number of planets, which can feel repetitive over time. The plot that provides an excuse to do all that racing sometimes feels shallow, as well. But where single-player racers are concerned, they don’t get much better than this one.

The Hunting Wives Season 2 Review: The Steamy Netflix Drama Hits The Mark Again
