  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • Recent findings suggest that earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated complications coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication glitch affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith says it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OpenAI’s recent release of Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 was widely panned. What happened?

Based on our data, it looks like they’ve been tuned for cost savings. Specifically output tokens per task and reasoning tokens per task have dropped.

Here is a chart of high-level cost change from the GPT-6 to GPT 6.2:.

Industry observers note that the X axis in the above chart is the ratio of spending of the GPT model compared to opponents in our battle system for real work. The Y axis on the above chart is Elo from our leaderboard.

The moves in the chart are significant, here’s the same chart with confidence intervals:.

Compared to opponents, Astra and Sol seem to be reasoning a lot less. Here is a chart of how much models reason compared to opponents in the same battle. Above the line means more reasoning and below means less.

You can see that both Astra 6 and Sol 6.1 were pretty normal models, but Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 become outliers.

We can see the same effect with output tokens:.

Sources indicate that are these changes significant? The p-value on output dropping is 0.0055 for Sol and 0.022 for Astra. The p-value on reasoning dropping is 0.00013 for Sol and 0.0064 for Astra.

In conclusion, Astra and Sol appear to be cost tuned compared to their predecessors, and to a degree that makes them underthinking outliers.

One of the most dramatic shifts in the AI landscape is the emergence of intelligent agents that can use iPhone and Mac apps in order to carry out tasks on our behalf.

Sources indicate that we can already use third-party chatbots in this way, and we know Apple is working hard to turn Siri AI into an agent. However, before the company even gets the chance, banks are already blocking them, and this may be just the start ….

According to recent reports, the science fiction promise of AI has always been to be able to tell a computer what we want done and have the task carried out for us automatically. That’s starting to turn into a reality with the emergence of AI agents.

We’ve already seen Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Muse gain agent capabilities, and Apple is expected to bring these to Siri AI at some point next year.

Earlier this month, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said that the company ultimately wants to go in this direction and may add these abilities next year. CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing Craig Federighi for faster software development, with specific mention of “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” which seems likely to mean agentic capabilities.

Last week also saw a since-deleted Apple job listing detailing aims for autonomous AI agents.

We’ve already seen some of the ways in which this can go wrong, and we recently outlined three significant risks. Wired reports that banks are now responding to these by either blocking AI agents or warning customers that using them can be dangerous.

Wells Fargo even goes as far as using capitals in its latest terms, stating that it will not be responsible for the consequences.

Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK.

We can likely expect similar pushback in sectors like online shopping as companies fear high returns costs and other consequences from mistakes by AI agents.

Recent findings suggest that personally, I don’t give any AI agents access to any of my banking or other financial services, considering the risks to be too high. I don’t see my position changing any time soon.

What’s your take? Would you trust an AI agent with access to your bank accounts? If not, would Apple launching agentic capabilities for Siri AI change your view? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • minipg is PostgreSQL as one executable, ready to use, with no server to configure.
  • According to recent reports, minipg embeds Docker Hub's postgres:18-alpine image and runs it with h9, used as a Zig library.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[ about | demo | using it | how it works | code | warning! | links ].

minipg is PostgreSQL as one executable, ready to use, with no server to configure. A .pgdb directory is the database: its data, config, credentials, and Postgres version all live inside it, and minipg app.pgdb opens a psql shell on it. A server starts when a command needs one and stops on its own when it's idle.

According to recent reports, minipg embeds Docker Hub's postgres:18-alpine image and runs it with h9, used as a Zig library. h9's Linux personality runs Alpine's own Postgres binaries directly on the host's hypervisor, with h9's Plan 9 kernel answering their system calls. There's no Linux kernel to boot, no VM image, and no Docker.

Industry observers note that the demo downloads about 35 MB. It needs JavaScript Promise Integration, which Chrome and Edge have from version 137; other browsers are getting it. It can also be opened on its own page.

The demo runs minipg's Linux build, which runs inside the Postgres image itself. It starts Postgres as ordinary processes and serves on a unix socket, since a page has no TCP. New databases come from a template cluster made at build time, because initdb takes half a minute on v86.

A .pgdb holds minipg.toml (settings and the generated superuser password) and pgdata/, Postgres's data directory as plain files. A stopped one can be copied like any directory. Latest clusters use Postgres's builtin C.UTF-8 locale, which sorts the same on every platform.

In CI, the Linux binary is static and needs no privileges or devices: without /dev/kvm, h9 runs Postgres on its native backend. A test job can be as small as:.

The README lists every command, and the manual is the full guide.

Exactly one process runs Postgres for a .pgdb, enforced by a lock. It holds the server's h9 machine, whose Linux root is the unpacked image and whose writable working directory is the .pgdb. The image's docker-entrypoint.sh initializes the cluster on first start. Commands never host Postgres themselves. If no server is running, they start one in the background and use it. psql, pg_dump, and the other tools each run in their own short-lived h9 machine (about 90 ms to start) over the same root.

Industry observers note that the source is on GitHub, under the MIT license. Building needs Zig 0.16, plus curl, jq, tar, and xz for the root:.

According to recent reports, minipg is early, and h9's Linux personality is young. On h9's native backend, Postgres is about 2x slower than native for one client, and slower under load. Don't trust it with data you can't recreate yet.

Recent findings suggest that this is a collection of preserved UI style guides a.k.a. interface guidelines from various companies, starting from the early 1980s and continuing to today.

In a recent development, many of the PDFs have been floating around, but I collected them in one place. Within each set, I tried to group them depending on themes and eras, and highlight the most vital ones. Some required more effort to find, I scanned a few myself, plus also created standalone mirrors of various minisites. Some of the mirrors were lightly cleaned up to make their consumption easier â stuff like pixellating images better, inlining images instead of linking to them, or fixing YouTube embeds. Enjoy!

In a recent development, (Commodore) Amiga was a multimedia personal computer particularly popular in the 1980s and 1990s in Europe. Its GUI was called Intuition and/or Workbench.

Sources indicate that android is a mobile operating system and a rival to iOS. The first style guide I could locate was in 2012.

BlackBerry was a beleagured maker of mobile handsets.

Common Desktop Environment (CDE) is a desktop environment for Unix machines, using (and eventually merging with) OSF/Motif widgets.

Common User Access (CUA) is a late 1980s standard for user interfaces that influenced Windows and OS/2.

Graphics Environment Manager (GEM) is a 1980s operating system/GUI. It was well-known by users of the Atari ST computers, known in these circles as TOS. Both of the websites mirrored are (obviously) more modern, but seem to contain vintage information, hence the confusing â1980s websiteâ label.

GNOME is a desktop environment for Linux and BSD operating systems. Note that the versioning number of these guidelines is very confusing.

Style guides for Googleâs early VR and AR efforts.

iOS (previously iPhone OS) is Appleâs mobile operating system for iPhone smartphones and their siblings.

Java is a programming language, which comes equipped with JFC (Java Foundation Classes) and Swing GUI components.

KDE originally stood for K Desktop Environment and is a popular Linux GUI.

Style guides for Microsoftâs motion sensing input devices.

These are some historical Apple GUI style guides, starting with Lisa in the 1980, and continuing to the âclassicâ Mac OS, with a brief stop in the Apple II corner.

More modern Apple Mac style guides, covering Mac OS X/Aqua and beyond.

An abandoned mobile operating system designed by General Magic.

Guidelines specific to Microsoft Office, in particular covering the use of its ribbon.

In a recent development, neXTSTEP was NeXTâs influential operating system and graphical user interface. It eventually morphed into OpenStep on one side, and modern Mac OS X on another.

Apple Newton was Appleâs PDA launched in 1993 and abandoned in 1998.

Nokia released various style guides for its early smartphones, including its Symbian operating system.

OPEN LOOK is a UNIX graphical user interface, started by Sun and AT&T.

Palm OS was the original graphical operating system for Palmâs mobile devices. Eventually, the company moved toward webOS, covered elsewhere on this page.

PenPoint was an early tablet operating system developed by GO Corporation for its unsuccessful line of devices.

RISC OS is a British operating system and GUI, developed originally for Acorn computers, and continuing as a community project.

Style guides for various UNIX-based operating systems from SGI, or Silicon Graphics Inc. Just like CDE above, these too use the Motif widgets.

An early 2000s joint venture between two companies that made mobile phones.

Sources indicate that taligent was a troubled software company, incorporated as an Apple/IBM partnership. One of its fruits was a CommonPoint application framework.

Industry observers note that webOS was a successor to Palm OS that was eventually purchased by HP and later LG Electronics. Today, it is used on smart TVs, refrigerators, and projectors.

Style guides for failed mobile Windows efforts, starting with Windows Mobile 6, and continuing through Windows Phone 7 and 8.

The Perfect Lord of the Rings Cast if It Were Made in 2026

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Lord of the Rings is the most totemic fantasy film franchise of all time.
  • The Lord of the Rings featured a wealth of actors, both seasoned and new, revitalizing the careers of some and launching others.
  • When it comes to the iconic villains in The Lord of the Rings, the evil lord Sauron is more of a presence than he is a persona.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Lord of the Rings is the most totemic fantasy film franchise of all time. Along with Harry Potter in the 2000s, it precipitated a revival of fantasy cinema that hasn't been matched since. It featured groundbreaking digital effects, incredible sets, miniatures, epic battle sequences, and an emotionally resonant storyline that gave all its technical wizardry purpose. Most of all, the franchise was cast perfectly.

The Lord of the Rings featured a wealth of actors, both seasoned and new, revitalizing the careers of some and launching others. Every actor fit perfectly into their role, and it's hard to imagine anyone else taking them over. But it's 2026, and the internet is the perfect place for wild speculation. While we continue to get new films and series set in J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth, with some roles recast and others played by the same actors, we also can't help but wonder what the original trilogy might have looked like if it were cast right now. If it were, this could be the perfect cast.

When it comes to the iconic villains in The Lord of the Rings, the evil lord Sauron is more of a presence than he is a persona. That leaves most of the acting to his underlings, none more prominent than the sorcerer Saruman. As played by the legendary Sir Christopher Lee in the Peter Jackson films, he exuded power and devilish deception. Any actor taking on the role of Sauron's right-hand wizard would need to have a similar sinister presence, and few can be as intimidating as Ralph Fiennes.

Industry observers note that sure, the English actor is already well known for playing the iconic wizard villain Voldemort in the Harry Potter films, but that shouldn't preclude him from playing another — it's not like Lee hadn't played other supernatural villains before he took on Saruman. Fiennes has a commanding presence, and there's little doubt he'd bring a chilling, distinct energy to the role. No two of his villain performances have ever been the same, and the three-time Oscar-nominated actor has the gravitas to rule Isengard.

It has been revealed that of near equal status to Fiennes and Lee is Sean Bean, an actor who was once best known for always dying on screen. That trend first came to prominence thanks to his role as Boromir, the human member of the Fellowship who fell prey to the temptations of the One Ring before valiantly sacrificing himself. It's a crucial role in The Fellowship of the Ring, requiring an actor who can elicit both sympathy and ire in equal measure.

According to recent reports, one does not simply recast a role played by Sean Bean, but in 2026, Theo James seems like he could do well in the role. While he was once pegged for bland leading man roles in franchises like Divergent, James has more recently found more success in roles that operate in grayer moral areas, including his Emmy-nominated turn in The White Lotus and Netflix's The Gentlemen streaming series. He's got the dashing looks of a hero, but the deceitful heart to go along with them, making him the perfect choice for the great warrior from Gondor.

Hotheaded and stubborn but fiercely loyal and honorable, Gimli became a fast fan favorite in the film franchise, mostly thanks to John Rhys-Davies' boisterous performance and his chemistry with Orlando Bloom. Any actor tasked with filling out the dwarven helmet of the character in 2026 would need to be able to recapture that same level of aggressive attitude without becoming abrasive. They'd also need to be able to rock a mean beard. Enter Matt Berry.

Sources indicate that best known to American audiences for his hilarious performance on the vampire series What We Do in the Shadows, Berry has a career of iconic characters to his name in British series such as Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The IT Crowd and Toast of London. He can elicit laughs in how he delivers a single word, and there's no doubt he'd be distinctly different yet just as memorable as Rhys-Davies as everyone's favorite dwarf.

Industry observers note that you can't have Gimli without his bromantic elf partner Legolas, a role that made a star out of Orlando Bloom. His ethereal male beauty and soft-spoken delivery made him perfect for the ageless character. While it seems like a role that any pretty blonde boy could be slotted into, there's a deceptive difficulty to the character. Too much personality, and he becomes too human; too much restraint and he becomes a bland bore. It's a fine line that an actor would have to walk, and Jamie Campbell Bower seems like he could walk it.

It might be cheating to include an actor who's already been cast as an elf in The Lord of the Rings, since Bower has been cast as Celeborn for the third season of The Rings of Power, but there's no doubt he'd be on the shortlist for Legolas if the character were being cast in 2026. He's obviously got the look for the character, and his role on Stranger Things demonstrated he can modulate his emotions with quiet intensity. Put him alongside Berry, and a whole new bromance could be born.

Industry observers note that pippin is one half of the second most popular hobbit bromance in The Lord of the Rings. The troublemaker joined Frodo's quest to destroy the One Ring alongside his best friend Merry by mere accident, but he proved his heroism multiple times over across the trilogy. Billy Boyd brought plenty of comic relief to the role, which required a great deal of panicking, and if there's any actor who's recently shown their ability to elicit laughs in the face of danger, it's Austin Abrams.

Abrams broke through last year in Zach Cregger's Weapons as a frazzled drug addict, and he continued his streak of livewire performances this year in both Cregger's new film version of Resident Evil and the survival thriller Whalefall. Abrams can bring levity to even the most bizarre situations, and Pippin finds himself in several of those. Put him in some capri pants and give him some pipe weed, and he'd be right at home in Middle-earth.

Recent findings suggest that where there's Pippin, you're likely to find Merry, his hobbit compatriot who's maybe just a half step ahead of his friend. Dominic Monaghan had incredible chemistry with Boyd in the films, and the two actors have kept the bromance going outside the franchise, reteaming on stage, on television and co-hosting a podcast together. Abrams would need an equal partner, and Joseph Quinn seems like he could be his perfect Merry.

Quinn has been on an upward trajectory ever since his breakthrough role on Stranger Things, with roles in Marvel movies, horror franchises and an upcoming turn as George Harrison in Sam Mendes' four-part biopic of The Beatles. If he's willing to be "the quiet Beatle," then there's a good chance he'd be the perfect actor to bring out the best in the other hobbits.

It has been revealed that if there's one actor who seems irreplaceable in The Lord of the Rings cast, it's Sir Ian McKellen as Gandalf. He's the only actor to have received an Academy Award nomination for his acting in the franchise, and his combination of authority, compassion and wisdom made him as integral to the film as Alec Guinness in Star Wars. McKellen is an acting titan, and it would take another legend to handle the iconic role of Gandalf — Gary Oldman is that legend.

In a recent development, oldman successfully transitioned from his early character roles into Hollywood's favorite villain for over a decade before becoming a steady mentor in franchises like The Dark Knight and Harry Potter. His added years only make him more suitable for the role now, and he'd bring a wholly different kind of wisdom to the role. If there's any actor who could command the same level of respect as McKellen in the role, it's Oldman.

Industry observers note that of all the members of the original Fellowship, Aragorn is the only one who already has a latest actor cast in the role in 2026. Jamie Dornan was recently revealed to take over the role from original actor Viggo Mortensen for the upcoming The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum. While it remains to be seen whether Dornan is able to acquit himself in the role and emerge from the shadow of Mortensen's star-making turn, there's no harm in suggesting another actor who might have also been a suitable fit for the role.

In a recent development, henry Cavill came on the scene as Zack Snyder's Man of Steel, and while the DC superhero franchise didn't give Cavill enough room to fly, he's proven his chops as a leading man elsewhere, and shown he knows how to swing a sword in The Witcher. With a little more salt added to his pepper, Cavill has the right amount of maturity to take on the role of the once and future king of Gondor, and would be more than adept at the requisite action scenes.

Industry observers note that the most loyal of all hobbits, Samwise Gamgee is one of the most likable fantasy movie heroes of all time. His unwavering loyalty to Frodo is matched only by his love of potatoes. The bond between the two hobbits formed the emotional backbone of the entire trilogy, and a great deal of that was due to the warmth that Sean Astin brought to the role. Any actor cast in the role now would need to be able to elicit the same amount of sympathy and likability. Fortunately, there's an actor who's already done that with another fantasy character named Sam.

John Bradley is best known for his role as Samwell Tarly on Game of Thrones, a character who shares more than a few traits with Samwise. It might seem like lazy casting, but sometimes an actor is simply built for a certain kind of role, and Bradley fits the bill for Sam. He has warmth and likability, and if he were cast as Samwise, he'd get to be more heroic, since one notably different trait of Tarwell was his cowardice. Casting Bradley as Frodo's faithful companion would be the perfect opportunity for him to be a hero.

It's the most key role in the entire trilogy. Frodo Baggins has the heaviest cross, or ring, to bear of any member of the Fellowship, and his suffering could easily become unbearable to watch if played by the wrong actor. Elijah Wood weaponized his innocent, youthful looks to really drive home how harrowed the character became over his journey, balancing the moments where the character is sympathetic and just plain pathetic. In 2026, there's one actor who could find that same level of innocence more perfectly than any other.

Sources indicate that josh O'Connor may have lost the role of James Bond, but it's arguable he's more suited to Hobbiton than Her Majesty's Secret Service. He's risen through the ranks in Hollywood thanks to his starring roles in films like Wake Up, Dead Man and Disclosure Day, both of which relied on his soft-spoken charm to play men who found themselves in over their heads. If that's not perfect for Frodo, then who is in 2026?

According to recent reports, upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

It has been revealed that samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

In a recent development, for anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

According to recent reports, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

Recent findings suggest that moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

For a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

In a recent development, sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

According to recent reports, for smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose indicates improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

Samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

Industry observers note that for something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That noted, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

If you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. That makes it particularly appealing for action movies and games, where directional sound adds to the experience.

The LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's right now $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

At just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That remarked, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Sources indicate that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

It has been revealed that black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

It remarked that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

It has been revealed that huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The Latest York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

It has been revealed that despite putting the tech giant at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, mentioned that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones said: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today revealed that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

It has been revealed that “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

It has been revealed that “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” stated Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

Recent findings suggest that as previously declared, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

  • It has been revealed that andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer states it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to massive issues.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

It has been revealed that andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he claims he has identified the next major shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

In a recent development, ng’s current efforts are focused on his company Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he indicates can yield “small data” solutions to major challenges in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

Recent findings suggest that the great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

Andrew Ng: This is a major question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having remarked that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

Ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a new paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

Ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

Recent findings suggest that having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of consumers, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing company with millions of users.

Recent findings suggest that ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from significant data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

It has been revealed that I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and noted, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing new here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

Ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and stated, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

Industry observers note that the data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one firm or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that revealed up.

Industry observers note that you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Sources indicate that ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from substantial data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

Recent findings suggest that when you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand upcoming model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having stated that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For substantial data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

In a recent development, for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very quickly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

Could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. New tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an important piece of the puzzle.

One of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

According to recent reports, ng: In AI, data cleaning is crucial, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention swiftly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

It has been revealed that for example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

In a recent development, ng: I think synthetic data is an important tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

Industry observers note that “In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion owners. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

Recent findings suggest that synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

To make these challenges more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a manufacturer approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

Ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

One of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

In a recent development, how do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

Ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. I find it really notable to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and upgrade the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

Industry observers note that in the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion users. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent upcoming neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s vital for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

According to recent reports, ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print glitch as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

Each model offers three selectable virtual screen sizes, depending on how immersed you want to be:.

GT Max’s wider field of view provides a more expansive picture, while GT offers a featherweight design. For travel, the appeal is simple: an immaculate 307-inch personal theater that slips right into your daily bag alongside your Apple gear.

Sources indicate that the GT Series also functions as an instant, private external display for a USB-C Mac. That makes the glasses invaluable far beyond streaming media, especially when you need an expansive, shoulder-surfer-proof dual-monitor workspace on a flight, train, or co-working desk.

Will Siri AI threaten Apple’s environmental target, given Google and Meta admissions?

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials.
  • All of this could potentially be put at risk by the firm’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….
  • Apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the firm’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

Apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The company has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

Overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the firm hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I said at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the organization’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

Sources indicate that after its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the company set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple said it was 95% of the way there.

Industry observers note that the tech giant also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and New Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

According to recent reports, potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

Back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai mentioned that the AI boom was “challenging” to the company’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the company is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are right now powered by Google’s Gemini models.

At the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

Recent findings suggest that more challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the company’s most recent environmental progress report, it noted that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

Recent findings suggest that we’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report said the organization had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

In a recent development, however, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

Recent findings suggest that what happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the tech giant moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

“AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li says. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the manufacturer will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the company’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

Do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

From's success is rare among TV indicates. The MGM+ horror-thriller began in relative anonymity but has become one of the most-watched shows after four years. When it premiered in 2022 on Epix — just before the network rebranded to MGM+ — the platform was a niche, relatively unknown streamer that many viewers only encountered as a Prime Video add-on. Yet, fueled by relentless word-of-mouth and glowing endorsements from the likes of Stephen King, From steadily built a fiercely loyal cult following. Over four seasons, that organic audience growth transformed the series into the most-watched original show in MGM+ history.

Created by John Griffin, the series captures a specific vibe of mystery that is hard to replicate without collapsing on itself. While many mystery highlights lose steam by piling on empty twists, From anchors its unknowns in a deepening lore that feels earned. Each season peels back another layer of the nightmarish town's curse, rewarding viewers without sacrificing its dread. Crucially, the mythology never overshadows the human element, thanks to excellent ensemble performances. Harold Perrineau delivers a career-best turn as Sheriff Boyd Stevens, alongside standout work from Catalina Sandino Moreno, Eion Bailey, David Alpay, and others.

The sleeper hit's trajectory then exploded into the mainstream when its first three seasons arrived on Netflix in October 2026. This exposed the show to an even bigger audience, and within weeks, the results started showing. From topped Nielsen's streaming charts with over five billion minutes viewed, proving the show's widespread appeal. As America celebrates Thanksgiving, From has received a massive boost on streaming and has surged to become the seventh most-watched show on the streamer in the US. Globally, it is the third most-watched show, behind the new horror hit The Body and the true-crime documentary The Trials of Karen Read. Meanwhile, From is preparing for one final season that ties everything together.

In April 2026, MGM+ confirmed that the hit horror-thriller had been renewed, but would end with Season 5. Principal photography kicked off in Halifax, Nova Scotia, in July 2026 and recently wrapped in late November, officially moving the final chapter into post-production. While MGM+ has yet to lock in an exact premiere date, the fifth season is slated to arrive in 2027. With the show's recent explosive success on Netflix, the final season is poised to be its biggest yet.

Watch the first three seasons of From on Netflix and the fourth on MGM+. Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.

I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that concern went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some consumers will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

It has been revealed that these new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple states it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:.

Sources indicate that I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

According to recent reports, one reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is important to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

#131494. iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (871 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (871 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it launched in 2017.
  • With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch.
  • In a recent development, the setup is simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it launched in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories.

With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 ($149, reg. $249) experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios.

In a recent development, the setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Sources indicate that once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

As a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though.

GymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

Industry observers note that airPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running.

Apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2.

Sources indicate that iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home.

It also gives iPhone and AirPods users a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers.

In testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t update as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data.

My sample 16-minute treadmill walk showed 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch.

I had been getting the impression that gym equipment manufacturers had been abandoning GymKit support - if they ever had done so initially. I even got the impression that the majority of equipment in Apple's own onsite Gym at the Apple Park may not have supported it - at least originally.

Does Apple have a webpage listing compatible brands and models? Like they do/did for HomeKit.

What is other people perception? Any rowing machines that support it?

…checks - surprisingly it looks like Peloton do support it on their bikes.

Industry observers note that if I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch.

Industry observers note that airPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data.

GymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way.

But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics.

A Lean 4 proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, built on Mathlib and using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

With its intriguing plots, fantastic production, and well-designed characters that leave an impact, Netflix has rolled out several great highlights this year. While there has not been a monumental rise in critical quality, the streamer’s lineup of shows has been much stronger and more positive than its original movies.

On the one hand, the streaming service has released multiple fresh fresh originals like The Boroughs to cure the Stranger Things hangover. At the same time, the year has also seen the returns of acclaimed shows like Beef and Black Doves, which have thrilled fans even more than last time. So, before we close the book on this year, here’s our ranked selection of the top 10 best Netflix shows of 2026.

It has been revealed that based on the American literary classic by Laura Ingalls Wilder, Little House on the Prairie follows the Ingalls family, parents Charles (Luke Bracey) and Caroline (Crosby Fitzgerald), and their daughters, Laura (Alice Halsey) and Mary (Skywalker Hughes), as they move from Wisconsin to a newly developing settlement in Kansas to start a new chapter for the family. Developed by Rebecca Sonnenshine, the Netflix original series marks the third television adaptation of the beloved book series.

Industry observers note that heavily compared to the NBC classic, Little House on the Prairie has had mixed reviews since it premiered in the summer of 2026. The show earned praise for its grounded historical context and sweeping visuals and period-accurate aesthetic, but has also been criticized for lacking the gritty realities of frontier life that the older adaptation captured so well.

Sources indicate that among the first major releases of 2026, Netflix’s Regency-era epic romance drama returned with an all-fresh fourth season, based on the novel An Offer from a Gentleman, the third in Julia Quinn’s titular novel series. Bridgerton Season 4 follows a classic Cinderella-inspired romance centering on Benedict Bridgerton (Luke Thompson) and Sophie Baek (Yerin Ha).

Industry observers note that after a divisive third season, Bridgerton Season 4 was a welcome return for the show, which has become a global streaming sensation since its premiere in 2020. The new chapter brings back the high-stakes, slow-burn romance narrative that has defined Bridgerton as a sensation of modern romance television. Critics and reviewers have praised Bridgerton Season 4 for its emotionally grounded storytelling, compelling romance plot, and better visual aesthetic compared to its previous seasons.

It has been revealed that two years after its first season premiere, The Gentlemen, Guy Ritchie’s black comedy crime drama reboot of his 2019 film returns for an action-packed, explosive second season, as Duke Edward “Eddie” Horniman (Theo James) deepens his grip on this underground cannabis business. As Eddie transforms into a ruthless power player in tandem with Susie Glass (Kaya Scodelario) and her father, Bobby (Ray Winstone), he finds himself facing new rivals and the consequences of unlimited ambition.

Sources indicate that though the new season arrived after a two-year gap, The Gentlemen Season 2 makes it worth the wait for fans and offers everything you expect from a Guy Ritchie caper. In fact, the second season of the crime thriller is darker, sharper, sleeker, and more high-stakes than the first. The second season of The Gentlemen trades the lighthearted, absurd tone and style of Season 1 for a punchier, snappier second chapter in Eddie’s evolution, while maintaining the original visual flair and cinematic style.

In a recent development, lee Sung Jin’s multi-award-winning black comedy anthology returned this year with a second season featuring an all-newly introduced cast in a new story of class satire and the unpredictable human condition. Beef Season 2 explores the escalating feud between couples Ashley (Cailee Spaeny) and Austin (Charles Melton), employees at an elite country club, and their boss and his wife, Josh (Oscar Isaac) and Lindsey (Carey Mulligan). After Austin and Ashley see the latter in a questionable confrontation, it sets off a wild story of blackmail, sabotage, and coercion, upending everyone’s lives.

Sources indicate that after the raw and unabashed exploration of rage and existential crisis that Beef introduced in its first season, the second season expands to a more philosophical and spiritual exploration of human nature. Created by Haley Z. Boston, Something Very Bad is Going to Happen is a horror-thriller miniseries that tells the story of a newly engaged couple, Rachel (Camilla Morrone) and Nicky (Adam di Marco), who are all set to get married. In the week leading up to the wedding, Rachel begins to experience several sinister, supernatural events that turn her wedding stress into a dark nightmare, making her seriously question her decision.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most highly anticipated horror series of 2026, Something Very Bad is Going to Happen puts an eerie psychological and supernatural spin on pre-wedding jitters. The dark gothic horror drama has been praised for its atmospheric tone and surreal treatment, which takes inspiration from horror classics like Rosemary’s Baby.

An adaptation of Jo Nesbø’s novels featuring the titular central character, Detective Hole is a gritty Nordic crime drama that follows the homicide detective, a brilliant but troubled man who is in search of a horrific serial killer. Starring Tobias Santelmann as Detective Hole, the series follows his relentless and often dangerous attempts to catch the killer while also trying to bring his corrupt fellow officer, Tom (Joel Kinnaman), to justice.

Recent findings suggest that directed by Oystein Karlsen and Anna Zackrisson, Detective Hole is a grim but stylish crime thriller with unexpected plot twists that can keep you hooked from start to finish. Intricate and intense, Jo Nesbø’s Detective Hole is a deeply layered serial killer mystery any genre fan would love.

Debora Cahn’s political thriller series returns for a fourth season that somehow manages to improve upon the first three excellent installments. Keri Russell and Rufus Sewell lead the show as Kate and Hal Wyler, a couple who attempts to juggle a marriage that’s often just as complicated as diplomacy. Things are more complex than ever this time around, as President Grace Penn (Allison Janney) begins making riskier and riskier moves, and a new Prime Minister in the form of Bethan Vaughn (Jodie Whittaker) throws alliances into question.

In a recent development, the Diplomat Season 4 has earned rave reviews from critics, presently holding an impressive 97% on Rotten Tomatoes. Janney’s shocking but well-deserved Emmy win this year seems like it could be the first of many more accolades in the show’s future. Season 4 both tackled the fallout from last season’s jaw-dropping cliffhanger and introduced a new twist in the finale’s last moments; needless to say, Season 5 can’t come soon enough.

Recent findings suggest that starring Alfred Molina, Geena Davis, Bill Pullman, Alfre Woodard, Clarke Peters, and Denis O’Hare, The Boroughs is a sci-fi adventure involving a group of residents at a retirement community out in the deserts of Latest Mexico. When a new resident named Sam (Molina) witnesses the shocking death of a fellow retiree and begins investigating, his search leads him to an unearthly, uncanny conspiracy that threatens the lives of the residents in the seemingly perfect community.

Executive produced by the Duffer Brothers and developed by Jeffrey Addis and Will Matthews, The Boroughs is a great follow-up to the Duffers’ five-season sci-fi epic. But the show surpasses its perception of “Stranger Things with older adults” and stands on its own merit as a heartfelt exploration of later-life challenges told as a chilling sci-fi mystery. The series has been widely praised for its standout cast, poignant storytelling, and excellent production values.

In a recent development, zoe Kazan's East of Eden is undeniably one of the best shows of the year. The adaptation of John Steinbeck's epic 1952 novel, the show centers around the Trasks and the Hamiltons, two families whose lives intersect in California's Salinas Valley. The novel takes heavy inspiration from the story of Cain and Abel, tackling complex themes of good versus evil.

Florence Pugh’s performance as Cathy Ames is widely considered one of the best in her career, which is saying something considering she has everything from Midsommar to Little Women on her resume. The rest of the cast, which includes Christopher Abbott, Mike Faist, Hoon Lee, and Ciarán Hinds, is impressive in their own right. The series earned 6.5 million views in its first four days alone and only increased in popularity over time, solidifying itself as one of the year’s most enduring hits.

Joe Barton’s genre-bending spy thriller returned this year after a two-year interval for a brand-newly introduced season with Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw reprising their roles as spies from the titular agency, Helen and Sam, respectively. In Black Doves Season 2, the duo faces new threats after discovering a conspiracy involving their handler, Reed (Sarah Lancashire). At the same time, Helen finds herself on increasingly uncertain ground after her husband becomes the Prime Minister. The new season also adds Ambika Mod, Neve Campbell, Babou Ceesay, and Samuel Barnett to the cast.

Black Doves Season 2 has proved itself to be darker, sharper, and faster than the first season, with higher stakes and a higher comedic quotient. While the upcoming season successfully maintains the show’s original themes of love, friendship, and espionage, it arguably lacks the moodiness and charm of classic British spy thrillers, which Season 1 achieved excellently. Despite that, Black Doves Season 2 has earned rave reviews, surpassing the acclaim of the previous season, with critics praising the more grounded plotlines and Knightley and Whishaw’s chemistry.
